children.text: Jackie DC is a solid happy hour spot in Navy Yard.

At $9 cocktails we were able to work through almost the entire drink menu without breaking the bank — major win. Server Young kept it attentive and informative. children.text: The Frost Bank Center in San Antonio, TX, delivers a fantastic game day. We loved the ample food selections; our loaded hot dog was divine, & the frozen cocktail hit the spot. negatives: While the hotel looks nice from the street, it's lobby is small. The car port is one lane & can hold maybe 3 SUVs before spilling into the street, a concern during weekend rush.
The 2 Queen room at the Thompson San Antonio Riverwalk is small for 2 adults and has only 1 drawer. This hotel would be hard to utilize for a longer stay due to space constraints.
We were not offered their welcome amenity beverage nor were provided any special Globalist in-room welcome amenity.
The shower water pressure was lower than preferred.
There is one small table in between the beds with one power outlet. There is another power outlet by the desk in the room under the TV and that's all we found. Definitely needs more power outlets.
In room stocked mini fridge is not useable for personal items, and the temperature was lukewarm at best. There was a note to contact guest services for a cold fridge.

The room has maintenance issues: the light attached to the bed had a short & comes on randomly & is protruding from the base. The room deadbolt is off center to the lock and has to be jimmied into place.

$25 daily destination fee (& tax) is a scam as there are no inclusions. Link here: https://www.hyatt.com/thompson-hotels/en-US/satth-thompson-san-antonio/policies

Destination Fee

The room has no central ceiling light & is dark at night. The room did not have an iron or iron board. There was a steamer offered.
positives: Thompson San Antonio Riverwalk offers a house car that we were able to use for a nearby drop-off which was nice.

Our 2 Queen room has a very tall ceiling, was close to the elevator. There is a water station (still, sparkling) along with ice near the elevators that can be refilled with complimentary water bottles.
There is a nice outdoor space on the 20th floor next to the indoor cafe, which we used as a coworking space.
Globalist breakfast ($60 per day) was good. We were able to get a entree and coffee each with the amount. Note the menu is limited.
The gym had lots of equipment along with bottled water although the space is rather small.
The 76ers NBA team was staying in the hotel & we were able to watch them walk onto the buses and sign autographs.
seoExcerpt: Staying at Thompson San Antonio Riverwalk? We loved the house car and 20th-floor workspace. See our full review of this family-friendly stay right here.
title: Thompson San Antonio - Riverwalk Hotel Review

children.text: The Thompson San Antonio – Riverwalk delivers an upscale vibe and excellent Globalist value, but it falls short on room functionality.

As an elite benefit, the $60 daily breakfast was high quality, and the 20th-floor terrace served as an excellent, scenic coworking space. The floor hydration stations and house car drop-off added great convenience, and catching the Philadelphia 76ers boarding their team buses in the lobby was an unforgettable bonus.

However, the 2-Queen room is tight for two adults. With only one drawer and a severe lack of outlets, it is impractical for longer stays. We also encountered maintenance issues, including a finicky deadbolt and a bedside light that shorted out randomly.

Furthermore, the $25 daily destination fee promises welcome drinks and daily fresh fruit—neither of which were offered or available. Missing these details, along with the lack of an in-room Globalist welcome amenity, misses the mark for a luxury brand.
The Takeaway:
A solid, stylish choice for a quick weekend or a remote-work base, but less than ideal if you require room space, storage, or flawless room maintenance.

negatives: Check-in agent was abrupt & did not provide any information about the hotel. Minimal interaction with other hotel staff.

Le Labo bathroom amenties in full size bottles. There was note that said a $120 charge would be added to folio if bottles were removed from the room.

Fast internet (110 Mbps).

negatives: Have to walk through the casino to access lobby, tram & restaurants
Walls are thin, can hear neighbors & people in the hall.
No bottled water offered (even with M gold status).
While the room has a coffee maker, the coffee cups & sugars were extra. Thankfully we travel to Vegas with our own travel kettle, coffee cups, teas & sweeteners.

The hotel did not have a texting feature. Anytime we had questions, we had to join the line at the front desk to speak to someone.
positives: Large lobby with ample seating.
Spacious room with double vanity, shower, and tub.
Close to Allegiant Arena (we walked over to attend a Raider game).
Easy access to Michelob Arena (located inside the hotel).
The front desk agent was polite & provide ample information about the hotel.

The front desk agent notified us that they wanted to confirm we were okay with the two queens as we had booked a king room prior to assigning the higher floor room.
Prior to checkout, I had questions about my bill and while the front desk agent was unable to provide clear information, their supervisor was professional and answered my questions in depth.
Spacious gym with lots of equipment.

The hotel has two elevators to access rooms. The main elevator for the lower floors always had a line, while the elevator (floors 56 to 62) to access our room on the Stay Well floor was never busy. Also, the hotel renumbered the floors after the 2017 shooting, floors 31 - 34 are now floors 56 to 59.

Crockfords Las Vegas

negatives: The room did not have a luggage rack.
There was no keycard needed to access the elevator.
Some time out of the ordinary for the Hyatt brand: there was no contact via text feature. On Saturday night we rang the front desk several times to nonresponse.
The wifi timed out each day, needed to log in on all devices each day. Would have preferred an option to stay logged in for the entirety of our stay.

positives: Ample seating in the lobby.
Attentive and personable staff: everyone we encountered was pleasant.
Quiet hotel in the financial district.
Close to the Wall Street subway station.
Received a complimentary upgrade to a spacious corner Centric Suite with several large windows & high ceilings.
The hotel has 6 elevators and there was rarely a wait during our 4 night stay.
Large shower/tub combination with a deep soaker tub.
The gym was a decent size however it was rather warm. The door was propped open and there were several portable fans plugged in.
Electronic blackout curtains have partial open capability.
The room had ample power outlets in convenient locations.
There were two large TVs in the room. The one near the bed allowed easier access to the HDMI port.
The room had a fridge for personal items (albeit missing a shelf).
Requested coffee machine & it was delivered quickly to the room.
The hotel offered free coffee on the "R" level during breakfast hours.
Globalist breakfast credit was $90 each day, nonetheless the full amount each day (up to $100) was comped.

Interestingly, three days before check-in a Centric Premier Suite was added to the list of available rooms. Marriott

negatives: The hotel gym is small & in the basement. There were 2 treadmills & small section of free weights.
The hotel doors don't have a slow-closer which resulted in constant door slams.
The wiew from the room was into the office building next door. We kept the blinds closed during office hours.
Sauna hours were weird. At check-in was told it was 6 - 10, which I thought was 6 am to 2200, however it is actually 1800 to 2200.
At check-in, the front desk agent wrote the wrong room number on the key cards. When we went to the room (504) the door would not work. I checked the Marriott app the room was listed as 304.
positives: Location: "easy" 10-minute walk from the train station. Note: The sidewalk is cobblestone for some portion & other portions are on an uphill.
Gym has sauna, open for limited hours.
Good assortment at the buffet breakfast, tasty pastries and ample juices.
Very comfortable bed, the best sleep we had during our Europe trip.
Staff was very responsive to message requests. Reached out about emptying the mini bar & they came within 5 minutes.
We liked the overall eclectic hotel vibe, interesting color scheme (red & black) with fun art.
Great price. We booked early & reserved our 3-night stay for €618 under their "Stay Longer on Us with Breakfast" special.
seoExcerpt: Staying at Hotel U14 in Helsinki? We loved the breakfast pastries and proximity to the park. Read our honest review of the walk and gym amenities here.

negatives: Light switches were hard to understand & some rooms don't have their own controls (bedroom closet can only be turned on when all the lights are on)
Bed was on the firm side, wished it was more plush.

Hotel gym is small. More than 4 people in it at a time can feel cramped. They have mats for stretching but there is minimal floor space to be able to use. Hotel gym is open 24 hours and accessible via keycard.
Hotel (infinity) pool is small, with 5 - 7 chairs available. There is a small, separate, wading pool for children.
Hotel is expensive for what it offers.
Residence and hotel mix might cause confusion. Two elevator system can disorient guests.
Suite layout is strange, you have to walk through the bedroom to access the living room.
No locking system doors, notable for the main bathroom which might be a privacy issue for some.
There was no easy way to contact front desk from the app. Would love to see a Whatsapp message option rather than having to call or visit front desk.
positives: Location: central location. 30-minute walk to Gardens by the Bay with a bus stop a block away.

Flashing light from smoke detector was bright during the night.

negatives: Keycard is not needed for the elevator which is a safety concern.

The hotel only has 2 elevators, which results in long wait times in the mornings.

[January 2025] One elevator was out of service during our stay. There was a note in the lobby which called it an "elevator project". Expect longer wait times during 8 - 10 am and 3 - 5 pm.
Room is small at 195 square feet; hard to navigate with 2 adults and luggage.
We were "upgraded" to a city view room however, our room looked into the buildings across the street.
During the mornings the housekeeping door nearby creaks very loudly when accessed which happened very frequently.

Breakfast service while good intention was slow & the server forgot several items. One party's food came out almost 5 minutes after the first plate was dropped off. After eating here the first day (Globalist benefit) we skipped it as there are ample food places within walking distance.

positives: Good location in Midtown Manhattan, close to everything & anything.

Comfortable King-size bed.

negatives: TV streaming (YouTube) randomly signed out and the two remotes were sluggish.

negatives: Bathroom soaps are generic Hyatt Regency brand wall-mounted pumps. Would have preferred a higher brand for the hotel.

Room Amenities (5): Nespresso machine, tea kettle, coffee cups with saucers, and two sizes of glasses. Bathroom amenities included 2 Robes, slippers, combs, brushes, toothbrushes, bath salts & a vanity kit.

Hotel Gym (5): The gym is large with treadmills, free weights, and lots of rep-counting machines along with a workout room. Concierge told us that the hotel offers a personal trainer however we never tried it out. Changing room

Breakfast in the Dining Room was delicious. Offering an extensive variety of local and international cuisine. Each day had different chef specials. As a globalist, I was offered the opportunity to order off the a la carte menu as well as select items from the buffet.

Crockfords Las Vegas

negatives: The large lobby has plenty of seating however no available outlets. Wifi in the lobby was 10 Mbps.
There were only two agents checking people in during the two hours we were in the lobby waiting for our room. Note: At 3 pm there were 4 front desk agents checking people in.
No lobby partitions for lines, which caused a random cluster of people, unsure of the line order to speak with the front desk.
TV streaming functionality would randomly drop the connection & show what was on live TV rather than what was streaming.
The bathroom door swings in, infringing on the already small water closet.
The bathroom does not have a rain shower. The showerhead in the bathroom looked old in comparison to the newer handheld component.
Unlike other hotels, the automatic shade cannot be opened partially. Click once to open, clicking while it is opening triggers it to close. I was unable to find a way to open the blinds partially.

As a Hilton Honors member, the breakfast credit could only be used at Dawg House which was a horrendous experience. First, after we ordered we were told it would be a 45-minute wait. Second, our food was extremely salty. Definitely recommend folks skip the Dawg House.
The rideshare pickup is a 10-minute outdoor walk from the Conrad lobby. Other hotels, like Mandalay Bay, have closer rideshare locations.

Same Resorts World cons across the 3 hotels:
• The gym is open from 5am to 8pm. Which we found out when we tried to access at 11pm. Such a weird time for this massive resort located in a city full of nightlife.
• There was no text feature (either with the hotel directly or via the Hilton app). We had to join the check-in line for simple inquiries, which sometimes resulted in a 15-minute wait to speak to someone.
• The daily $45 resort fee includes (spoiler, nothing): "Guest internet access; smart TV casting ability; 10% off spa or fitness retail; 5% off spa or fitness treatments; 5% off cabana experience; 5% off 2 pool chair experience; unlimited local and toll-free calls."
• The hotel does not provide a complimentary airport shuttle service (which could be included in the daily $45 resort fee).

After checking out I noticed I was charged twice by Resorts World. When I was checking in I noted to the front desk agent that I was charged twice after our Conrad stay. He noted that they would be vigilant to ensure that did not happen at Crockfords, yet it did.

Quiet floor, we did not hear neighbors from the room during our sold-out. stay,

children.text: Before our stay, I read many reviews filled with disdain for the Crockford Las Vegas. After staying at the Hilton and Conrad I was pleasantly surprised at how much I enjoyed our time here.
Booked a two-night weekend stay in a Strip View Superior King Room via Amex Fine Hotels and Resorts for $562.94 which included a 25% nightly rate discount.
After staying at the three Resorts World hotels, for $250/night, I would definitely stay at the Crockford for better service, better amenities, and an overall better Resorts World stay.
Overnight stay at Chicago Athletic Hotel in a King Millennium View room. TL;DR great hotel close to Chicago Bean (or
Cloud
, if you call it that).

Normally we've flown to O'Hare when visiting Chicago; on this trip we flew to Midway and now I see why the locals prefer Midway. In the future, definitely making it a point to fly Midway over O'Hare, whenever possible. The ease of it when compared to the chaos of O'Hare is unmatched.

Upon landing, we walked for about 20 minutes to catch the Orange Line train to the hotel. Chicago Transit Authority (CTA) is running a sale on public transportation tickets until Labor Day 2021, saving us 50% on an all day pass ($5 per person, versus $10).

After a 45 minute train ride, we walked down to the street from the platform & walked one block to the side entrance of the hotel. Upon entering a gentleman pushing a baggage cart welcomed us & ushered us to the stairs to the lobby.

Check-in was fast & easy. I used a Hyatt Free Night Certificate to book this stay & in the app saw we were assigned a room on the 19th floor. Because of my Hyatt Globalist status we were "upgraded" to a King Millennium View Room on the 6th floor. I asked if the 6th floor had good views (
since I was originally assigned a 19th floor room
) and was told the original room on the 19th floor was an interior facing room, with no view.

We took our keys & headed up to the corner room located right off the elevator. I loved the dark tones throughout the hotel: from the black room door to the walnut colors in the elevator, it was definitely a vibe. The King Room was large for its 270 square foot size. The bathroom was spacious with a gorgeous marble double vanity.

We dropped our bags & headed downstairs to grab something to eat from the Shake Shack located on the ground floor. There was a line of around 5 people in front of us, which gave us time to review the menu & make our selections. Note: over the course of the next 24 hours, there was always a line at Shake Shack, sometimes stretching into the "faux" lobby and nearly touching the hotel customer service desk located there o on the ground level.
Our wait for Shake Shack was around 25 minutes
(line, ordering, waiting for food),

which was not too bad. Next time will try the in room dining option to compare wait times. Once our food was ready, we headed back up to the room to eat before heading out to the Art Institute of Chicago across the street.

One thing I loved about this hotel was it's proximity to activities - we were able to walk from the hotel to the Art Institute as well as through Millennium Park to get to Navy Pier. Within walking distance is a Magnolia Bakery, Target along with no shortage of restaurants.

Breakfast was served in the "Drawing Room", located right off the check-in counter. Service was prompt & the food was good. My only complaint was that I ordered over-hard (fried) eggs and was given scrambled eggs. When I started I ordered over-hard eggs, the waiter told me they were over-hard scrambled (
is that even a thing?
). Not wanting to argue any further, I took the food.

As a Globalist, breakfast is complimentary, nonetheless, upon check-out why our bill did not have the breakfast charge listed, my credit card showed the charge. When I brought this up to the Assistant Front Office Manager Christina, she told me the charge would drop off after a few days. Noting that the two are separate and the charge hold is necessary. She went as far as emailing me the next day to confirm the matter was resolved.
Overall this was another great Hyatt stay in a nice hotel in one of our favorite cities.

children.text: We found the Hyatt Place South Reno to be a bit of a mixed bag, but leaning towards positive with a few caveats. The location was fantastic for us, with easy access to shopping, dining, and the ski resorts. We also appreciated the affordable "Members Save More" rate and the clean environment throughout the hotel. The free parking was a nice bonus too!

However, we were disappointed that the service was lacking, particularly at the front desk where we encountered a rather disinterested agent. We also weren't given any information about the amenities, and to our surprise, the pool was closed without any prior notice. The Wi-Fi was advertised as high-speed, but we found it to be quite glitchy. The gym was uncomfortably hot, and we had some concerns about security with the elevator access.

Ultimately, we think it depends on what you're looking for in a hotel. If location and value are your top priorities, and you're willing to overlook some shortcomings in service and amenities, then it could be a decent choice. But if you're hoping for a seamless and well-rounded experience with attentive service and fully functional amenities, you might want to consider other options.

children.text: Hyatt Regency JFK Airport at Resorts World New York is a 4-star hotel located in Queens, New York. It is just a short drive from John F. Kennedy International Airport and is also home to NYC's only casino, Resorts World Casino New York City. The hotel offers a variety of amenities, including a restaurant, bar, gym, and casino. It also has a free shuttle service to and from the airport. The rooms are spacious and comfortable, and the staff is friendly and helpful. The Original Rinaldi's Deli and Cafe is a popular spot for sandwiches, salads, and breakfast in El Segundo and Los Angeles. They've been serving up delicious food for over 60 years, and their reputation for quality is well-deserved.

The sandwiches are the star of the show at Rinaldi's. They use fresh, high-quality ingredients, and their sandwiches are always made to order. The Italian combo is a classic choice, but there are plenty of other options to choose from, including the Reuben, the BLT, and the grilled chicken salad sandwich.

The salads are also very good at Rinaldi's. They're made with fresh ingredients, and they're tossed in a variety of dressings. The Cobb salad is a popular choice, but there are also other options to choose from, such as the Caesar salad and the Greek salad.
Rinaldi's also serves breakfast. Their breakfast sandwiches are made with fresh bagels, eggs, and cheese. They also have a variety of breakfast burritos and breakfast bowls to choose from.
The service at Rinaldi's is friendly and efficient. The staff is always happy to help you choose the perfect sandwich or salad, and they're always willing to make substitutions.
The prices at Rinaldi's are reasonable. Sandwiches start at around $7, and salads start at around $10.

Overall, The Original Rinaldi's Deli and Cafe is a great place to go for a delicious sandwich, salad, or breakfast. The food is fresh and high-quality, the service is friendly, and the prices are reasonable. I highly recommend it!

children.text: We had a delightful dining experience at Jasmine's Caribbean Cuisine. The atmosphere was warm and inviting, with a nice "Jamaican vibe." The staff was friendly and attentive, and the service was prompt.

We started with the Codfish Fritters, which were a bit different from what we're used to, but still tasty. The oxtail, however, was absolutely divine! The meat was fall-off-the-bone tender and perfectly seasoned. The plantains were also a hit, soft and flavorful.
The drinks were a highlight. We enjoyed the Coco Breeze and Scandal Rum Punch, both of which were refreshing and flavorful.

While the food was delicious, we did find the portions a bit small, especially for the oxtail. Also, the restaurant is quite small, so we recommend making a reservation to avoid a long wait. Overall, though, we had a great experience and would definitely return to try other items on the menu.

After we explored the Denver Zoo & Denver Museum of Nature & Science for five hours, we walked one mile through City Park to have dinner at Mono Mono Korean Fried Chicken.
Upon entering there was 1 waitress at the bar who instructed us to sit anywhere we liked.
After picking the only wet table in the restaurant, we picked a different table/booth combination against the back wall before settling in (aka removing cold weather layers.)

On the walk over, we decided to order so when the waitress came, after we were settled, by with waters, we promptly ordered Combo B, "mild", 86 the slaw, instead subbing for an extra piece of Texas toast.

During our Wednesday night visit, there were two other occupied tables: a table of two on the same wall of booths/table combos as well as a family of three in the middle booth. During our visit, these were the only 3 occupied tables. As we were leaving several more patrons entered the restaurant

While we waited for our food, we visited the bathroom to wash our hands, noting that it was stocked and relatively clean. Albeit noting both paper hand towels and toilet paper were set on the back of the toilet, rather than in their respective wall unit holders.

Our food arrived 20 minutes after we went to the bathroom, so around 25 minutes after ordering and we immediately asked for a to-go box, don't be fooled Combo B is a plethora of food. We portioned half of the food (chicken) in the to-go boxes and began to tackle the mountain of fries (cold fries are a "no-go")
I was surprised at how good all the food was, my favorite was the teriyaki soy followed closely by the saucy popcorn chicken.
Service was good, the one waitress managed the three tables well, ensuring we each had everything we needed. She was always within earshot if anything came up during our meal.
One negative was that I asked for a cup of hot water (to make a cup of tea) and she stated they did not have water (even at the bar) but could ask the kitchen to boil a cup for me, which I declined.
Overall a great experience, with great food at a very reasonable price.

EMBARCADERO location to grab a late lunch/early dinner. Have you ever been so hungry you ordered way too much food? Yeah, that's what happened to us. In hindsight, the Taco Box would have been more than enough. Somehow we misunderstood that the "Taco Box" of 4 tacos and nachos was meant to feed a family (
hence the name)
, thus it would have been plenty for both of us.

In addition to the "Taco Box", we ordered the "Smokey Pig Sandwich", which was delicious several hours later as a hotel late-night snack. With full bellies, we ventured back to the hotel, stopping to enjoy a beautiful San Diego sunset.
The next morning, we woke up & headed downstairs for breakfast. When we got off the elevator, there was a sign highlighting the
breakfast buffet options

We joined a line to check in & then waited to be seated. Although the area was filled, I must applaud the staff for having a system in place that kept things moving. We were in line for 11 minutes, before we were seated and the whole breakfast (joining the line, getting food, eating & closing out check) took 57 minutes. We arrived at breakfast at 10 am, and in the future, would recommend coming closer to 1045 as when we left, there was no line to check-in & the dining hall was about half full. After being seated outside (per our request), we ventured back inside to join the omelet station line. This is the only station where staff served patrons, in the time of COVID I would have preferred for the hotel to have staff still serving patrons all dishes rather than the current self-serve model. At a minimum for the hotel to offer patrons disposable gloves to use to touch the tongs. At $32 per person, the breakfast buffet was lacking, as a Globalist this was included in our stay at no additional cost, so I did not feel too bad about just getting an omelet with orange juice.

After breakfast we took a stroll to explore the area, stopping at Extraordinary Desserts, and stumbling upon a sort of farmer's market back in Embarcadero. With a 4 pm check-out, we were then off to our second San Diego hotel, the Andaz San Diego.

gallery.alt: Room

negatives: Buffet breakfast was limited & pricey, costing $32/per person plus tax. During COVID it was also uncomfortable to watch throngs of people handle the same tongs.
Small bathroom with shallow tub & sink
The bed was meh (3/5), the pillows were lumpy & did not provide adequate support.
positives: Great service: Jasmine at check-in was professional, courteous & helpful.
The hotel has several restaurants & a lobby store with snacks
Good location close to the marina, with tons of restaurants & activities nearby.
seoExcerpt: Staying at Manchester Grand Hyatt San Diego? Jasmine at check-in was so helpful. Great marina location, but is it worth the price? Read our full review.
title: Manchester Grand Hyatt San Diego Review

children.text: I've come to realize my sweet spot for hotels is 200 - 600 rooms. The boutique feels with enough amenities to make things enjoyable. With a great location & awesome staff, the more than 1,600-room Manchester was just too big for me.
We used a free night certificate for this stay, as rates for the night were upwards of $600. If given the choice I might look to stay somewhere else in the same area in the future.

negatives: Blackout curtains let in some light.
The room is small (~200 sq feet) & would be hard to maneuver with large checked suitcases & more than 2 adults.
You can hear hallway chatter & door closures.
The shower took a long time to heat up, we had to leave it running for a few minutes. It might be an issue during the winter months.
Slow Internet speed (8 mbps)
positives: Value: $200-night hotel close to Barclay's Center, booked last minute.
Friendly staff: Miracle at the front desk was very personable. We checked in via the app however our digital key was not working & had to get physical keys when we arrived.
Amenities: The hotel basement has a 24-hour workspace/game room, which also houses the small gym & offers complimentary coffee & tea.
Nearby shops: There are plenty of restaurants & shops nearby, notable Starbucks is a block away.
Comfortable bed
seoExcerpt: Need a budget spot near Barclays Center? Our Tru by Hilton Brooklyn review covers the $200 rate and cool game room. Did our digital key work? Read more.
title: Tru by Hilton Brooklyn Hotel Review

children.text: We needed a hotel within walking distance of Barclay's & after initially booking a stay at the nearby TownePlace Suites, we saw the Tru was on the same block & for $200 less during our trip, so we switched. We've stayed at a Tru before & know they are a bare-bones Hilton brand which was perfect for our 2-night stay.
Check-in: After getting off at the Foggy Bottom  GWU Metro stop, we walked through GWU to head towards the hotel.
Upon arrival, there was no bellman at the door. As we let ourselves in, David from the front desk was walking towards us asking if we needed assistance with our luggage.

At the check-in desk, David noted were had been upgraded to a Park Junior Suite (also noted in the Hyatt app) on the 8th floor. We asked if the assigned room 1) had a view and 2) was a connecting room. David found us a new room on the 6th floor with a view however noting it was a connecting room. He was persistent & continued to search & finally found us a Park Junior Suite, with a view & a non-connecting room. David handed us two keys & directed us to the elevator.
Upon entering the room, the phone rang. It was David checking to see if we needed anything & informing us to call the front desk with any issues.
At 17:35 we called the front desk to see if there were any reservations available at Blue Duck Tavern & we were able to get an 1800 reservation.
This was a great way to start a great three (3) night's stay.

"Park Hyatt Washington D.C. is located in the West End neighboring Georgetown, Pennsylvania Avenue, and the White House. Savor Michelin distinguished food in Blue Duck Tavern while sipping exceptional wines, as you watch a dramatic culinary presentation in the open kitchen and wood-burning Molteni oven." - Park Hyatt

negatives: Windows need to be soundproofed, could hear street noise from the 9th floor.
The pool & gym are located on the "M" (2nd) floor however hotel signage says it is on the 3rd floor, which was a bit confusing.
The suite had a barn door between the living & bedroom, wish there was a locking door.
positives: Amazing, attentive staff.
Spacious Corner Park Junior Suite
In-room stocked Nespresso with green & black tea capsules
Fast, reliable WiFi (63 MB)
Globalist breakfast credit is $90 & we were able to sample many items from the menu during our 3-night stay.
seoExcerpt: Staying at Park Hyatt Washington D.C.? We loved the spacious corner suite and Nespresso in our room. Read our honest review of this D.C. hotel stay here.
title: Park Hyatt Washington D.C. Review

children.text: We spent $650 booking a 3rd-night free stay at Park Hyatt DC. Booked a 1 King Bed and was upgraded to a Park Junior Suite.
With a Georgetown location, great staff & delicious hotel restaurant Blue Duck Tavern, we would definitely stay here again.

"This straightforward hotel set next to Harrisburg International Airport is 7 miles from Indian Echo Caverns and 4 miles from Frey Manor Park.

The relaxed rooms feature free Wi-Fi, flat-screen TVs and minifridges, plus microwaves, and tea and coffee-making facilities. Upgraded rooms add living areas.

Breakfast is complimentary (grab and go). Other amenities include a bar and a gym. Free parking is available."

negatives: No airport shuttle. It is a 5-minute partially covered walk from the hotel to the airport. With inclement weather, this could be a problem with luggage.

When we arrived we noticed that 75% of 2nd floor rooms were left partially opened, yet there was no housekeeping cart in the hallway. About 30 minutes later, housekeeping emerged from one of the rooms.
The 2nd-floor ice machine was not working, went to the 1st-floor to get ice.
This is a new airport hotel where the total price was $131.65.
Not much nearby. There's a gas station across the freeway, however not many other food options.
positives: Close to Harrisburg Airport (MDT)
Available coin laundry. There was 1 washer ($1.75 for 30 minutes) and 1 dryer ($1.50 for 30 minutes)
Grab & go breakfast included: yogurt, muffin, fruit, bottled water, granola bar, & a mint.
In-room microwave & mini-fridge.
seoExcerpt: Staying at Fairfield Inn & Suites Harrisburg Airport? We used the coin laundry and grabbed breakfast before our game. See our full review of this stay here.
title: Fairfield Inn & Suites by Marriott Harrisburg International Airport Review

children.text: Good hotel near Harrisburg airport. Would stay here again to provide ease of access for early AM flights.

"Your stylish base in the cosmopolitan heart of London, Hyatt Place London City East is close to the vibrant Brick Lane, Spitalfields Market, Tower of London and the artistic streets of Shoreditch." -
Hyatt

negatives: Walls are thin: can hear folks in the hallway.
The room is small with no drawers to unpack suitcase. Instead there was a luggage rack propped in the corner upon arrival.
Hotel has a small windowless gym that was quite stuffy.
Wifi was on the lower end, a bit slow for such a densely populated area.

Not enough power outlets in the room. There was only one side table with one outlet. The desk, on the opposite side of the bed, has two outlets and then's there one by the front door, that we used when we needed to iron.
Location is sketch, walking through lots of homeless & trash.
positives: Location: close to Aldgate East & Whitechapel Underground stations. Close to many shops & restaurants. 10 minute walk to Spitalfields Markat & Shoreditch.
Upgraded to a room with a step-up balcony. Nice to have some outdoor space.
Bed was comfortable, able to get sleep; albeit it was on the firm side.
No noise from 9th floor rooftop bar.
Included breakfast (Globalist) was good. Limited rotation so after a few days it would become boring.
TV had built-in Chromescast that sporadically would drop off while watching a video.
Staff was very friendly & accommodating. Was given 12 pm early check-in.
Booked for 9k points per night, where similar rooms were £600 per night. Great value on points, although the room was small.
room: 1 King Bed High Floor w/ Balcony | Room 809
seoExcerpt: Staying at Hyatt Place London City East? We loved our balcony room and the easy walk to Spitalfields. Read our honest review of this London hotel stay.
title: Hyatt Place London City East Hotel Review

children.text: We need a central location, available on points for our 3-night stay. At 9k points per night, it was a steal of a deal. Staff is wonderful & it was a great base of a few days.
The Hyatt Regency Lake Tahoe Resort (Presidential Suite) is an 896-square-foot one-bedroom suite with separate lavishly appointed sleeping and entertaining space, plus a large dining/meeting table.

negatives: While spacious, the suite did not have a dedicated dining room table.
The bedroom barn door does not have a locking mechanism.
positives: Soft King-sized bed
65” HD TV in the bedroom and 65” HD TV in the living room
Cozy gas fireplace
Mini fridge and wine fridge provided
Large bathroom in the bedroom and half-bath in the living room
Wifi speed was excellent, no lags or issues while on Zoom meetings.
seoExcerpt: Staying at the Hyatt Regency Lake Tahoe in Incline Village? We loved the cozy gas fireplace in our suite. See if this room is worth the splurge for you.
title: Hyatt Regency Lake Tahoe Resort (Presidential Suite) Review

children.text: My new favorite room at my favorite hotel. The Presidential Suite is spacious, with two TVs, ample seating, and a large bathroom with double vanity & soaker tub. Great place to come back to after a day of skiing, or a cozy place to spend a snowy day indoors.

negatives: Check-in was short. While the front desk agent was nice, she was not aware of Hyatt Prive (no welcome letter) & did not mention my Globalist status benefits. She also pointed me to the elevator rather than walk me to it & didn't call 10 minutes later to check if everything with the room was ok.
The entrance smelled horrendous. Like they just put down mulch. By the 2nd day the smell has subsided & was minimal.
Text feature is not available on Whatsapp, a small feature that could cater to global audience.
The front entrance does not have a ramp, down the stairs to the front desk, an accessibility concern.
Welcome amenity was 1 bottle of still water & chocolate covered cherries with no note, so unsure who it was from.
The hotel did not send a prewelcome email asking about preferences prior to check-in.
positives: Booked a Park Executive Suite and was upgraded to a Georgetown suite on the 3rd floor.
Bed was very comfortable. Requested 2 additional pillows after check-in.
Large bathroom with double vanity, along with shower/tub combo.
Spacious corner suite with dining table (only 3 chairs), large sectional, 1.5 bathrooms and a separate workstation area. Lots of windows (that could open) which allows for ample natural light.
Globalist breakfast credit was listed as $60 per person. Total for 2 averaged $130 and all but the $5 room service delivery fee was removed.
seoExcerpt: We stayed at Park Hyatt Washington DC during our NBA trip. Our suite upgrade was great, and the bed was so comfy. See if it's worth the price here.
title: Park Hyatt Washington DC Hotel Review

children.text: Similar to our
last stay

, we booked a 3-night free stay, this time in a Park Executive Suite for $918 plus tax. Upgraded to a large corner Georgetown suite, we had more than enough space for our 3-night stay. The hotel is a good base 0.5 miles from the Foggy Bottom metro & walkable to Dupont circle. There are several hotels in the area yet the area is rather quiet & easy to navigate, would stay again.
The Hotel Indigo Harrisburg is located in a commercial area off Interstate 283, this informal hotel is 5 miles from the 1890 Walnut Street Bridge and 6 miles from Harrisburg International Airport.

negatives:
The staff was lackluster. The front desk attendant was short in responses & not attentive. I called prior to arrival to inquire if I would be able to check in early (at noon). The person on the phone said it would not be a problem. When I arrived & stated I wished to check in the front desk person stated rudely "Check-in is at 3 pm". I informed her that I had called in & was told I could check in early. With a sigh & brief typing on the computer, she stated "Oh, looks like your room is ready". 

 Walking through the hallways we were not acknowledged by the staff.
No COVID protocol. Staff was not wearing masks nor did they enforce patrons to. However, the hotel restaurant was closed due to "COVID", which seemed contradictory.
Question regarding the cleanliness of the room due to the two AC units being covered in dust & the dirty Keurig machine.
The outdoor pool was drained, likely closed for the winter season.
As an IHG Platinum member, I received no recognition of status.
The total price of $167.66 seemed expensive for the area. This hotel should be priced around $80 - $100 per night.
positives: Close to Harrisburg Airport (MDT), with a shopping plaza & restaurants across the street.
Executive King Room was spacious & kitchenette was equipped with a cold mini-fridge, microwave, Keurig coffee machine & sink.
seoExcerpt: Staying at Hotel Indigo Harrisburg? Our review covers the spacious Executive King room and handy kitchenette. See if this spot fits your next road trip.
title: Hotel Indigo Harrisburg-Hershey Review

children.text: If I was in the area in the future, I would choose a different hotel. The staff was apathetic & rude, the room while spacious was not clean & the price was too high.
One night was too long of a stay at the Hotel Indigo Harrisburg, PA.

"A magnificently beautiful, newly restored 1800s building in the heart of Vesterbro, Copenhagen. Kindness transcends the entire house and circulates from Grand Joanne into Vesterbro towards passionate, kind people – traveling or just looking for a place to hang out." -
Joanne

negatives: There were misses with small touches in the room: a robe but no slippers, a kettle but no coffee machine. The bathroom has toothbrushes but no wash cloths.
Room does not have a useable fridge. We were able store some items in the fridge behind the front desk.
Two elevator system to get to the room with luggage. The 2nd elevator is small & can only accommodate 1 person with luggage.
Room is expensive and the view is the inner workings of the hotel where staff is taking out trash & laundry.
Water temperate system is weird. The sink faucet only has 1 knob and you have to turn it all the way to the left to get hot water, same for the shower.
The bathroom is small, with a shallow sink resulting in water splashing everywhere.
Bathroom does not have any counter space.
Long hallway in the room is unusable space.
positives: Good location close to Copenhagen Central Station & Tivoli Gardens. There are plenty of shops and restaurants within 5 minutes in any direction.
The gym is large and has lots of equipment, albeit it is in the windowless basement.
Friendly staff that spoke English well.
You can text them via Whatsapp & they respond quickly.
The included breakfast was good with a variety of items during our 2-night stay.
seoExcerpt: Staying at Hotel Grand Joanne in Copenhagen? We loved the huge gym and central Vesterbro location. Read our honest review of this historic hotel here.

children.text: Skip the breakfast package & grab a hot dog from John's Hot dog deli near the train station.

title: Hotel Grand Joanne Hotel Review

children.text: Hotel Grand Joanne is a good base for exploring Copenhagen close to Copenhagen Central Station & Tivoli Gardens. Our two-night stay was pricey (5.422 DKK) and while the room was spacious, it had a small bathroom & view of hotel's trash. If I stayed here again in the future, I would book the Deluxe room (again) for a lower rate (under 2.000 DKK per night) without the breakfast option as there are many restaurants within walking distance.

Hyatt Place Dallas / Arlington is in the heart of Arlington’s Entertainment District, just steps from Six Flags Over Texas, and five minutes to Arlington’s famous AT&T Stadium. Our Dallas hotel makes it easy to check out a baseball game at Globe Life Park or catch a concert at Arlington’s newest attraction, TexasLive! Venue. -
Hyatt Place Dallas/Arlington

negatives: Internet is slow (5 mbps).
Both ice machines (3rd & 5th floor) were inoperable, we asked for ice at the front desk.
Hotel is located in an industrial part of town, behind the interstate and there is not much within walking distance: you will need a car.
Elevator jolts between floors which is concerning.
Keycard not needed to access room floors, a security concern.
Starting to show age & should be refreshed soon.
The wall AC unit is loud & has dust in the vent, a cleanliness issue.
positives: Staff is friendly & a welcome amenity was provided upon check-in.
Close to Six Flags.
The hotel offers complimentary breakfast.
Has an outdoor pool.
room: King High Floor (w/ Sofa Bed) | Room 617
seoExcerpt: Staying at Hyatt Place Dallas/Arlington? We loved the friendly staff and free breakfast near Six Flags. See if this budget stay is worth your trip.
title: Hyatt Place Dallas/Arlington Hotel Review

children.text: Built in 1996 and renovated in 2014, the Hyatt Place Arlington is a good 2-night (max) base for those going to Six Flags or AT&T Stadium. In the future, even with our 2-night stay costing a total of $250, I would stay elsewhere as there is not much food/activities available in the area & the hotel was just okay.

Park Hyatt New York is a luxury 5-star hotel in the heart of Midtown Manhattan, located directly across from Carnegie Hall and one block from Central Park. Spacious guest rooms and suites offer floor-to-ceiling views of the city and spa-like amenities. While in NYC, find serenity at Spa Nalai, take a dip in our hotel pool, explore our curated art collection or host an event in one of our unforgettable venues. -
Hyatt

negatives: The Living Room (main dining) seemed overwhelmed at 8am on a Thursday.
The room walls are thin. We could easily hear people walking outside
positives: Comfortable King-size bed, firm mattress with minimal partner motion transfer.
Great location near major attractions and Central Park
Attentive, courteous personable staff (not too stuffy).
Large gym with sauna & locker rooms.
The hotel has a small indoor pool with great views.
seoExcerpt: Staying at Park Hyatt NYC? We loved the firm mattress and prime spot near Central Park. See why this Manhattan stay was a hit for our family trip.
title: Park Hyatt NYC Hotel Review

children.text: This is a great hotel if you want to be close to Times Square.  You have access to a lot of stores, restaurants, and parks. With a great location near Central Park, along with personable staff and modern rooms, we will stay here (on points) again when in New York.

"A stunning fusion of modern design with stylish oriental flair, Mandarin Oriental, New York features elegant guestrooms and suites—all with breathtaking views of Manhattan and Five-Star hospitality." -
Mandarin Oriental

negatives: Not a fan of the yellow decor, the carpet was thick & made it hard to maneuver roller luggage.
No electronic controls for curtains and lights.
The bed had a spring mattress that had a high partner movement transfer which made it difficult to get a good night's sleep.
The curtains in the room don't keep out the sunshine that well.
The outlet is only located on one side of the bed.
The room had only one pair of slippers in them, so I had to request 2nd pair.
Limited in-room dining menu, for breakfast and dinner.
The small gym was not 24 hours, you needed to ask the front desk for access after 6 pm.
positives: The 50th-floor room had great views of the Hudson River.
Keycard is needed to activate the elevator.
Spacious bathroom with dual vanity, water closet, shower, and soaker tub.
Great location near Central Park West and Columbus Circle train station.
There was a yoga mat provided in the room.
Daily housekeeping and turn-down service.
Was able to get a 1 pm checkout (after some back and forth).
The room had robes and a Breville Nespresso machine.
seoExcerpt: Staying at Mandarin Oriental, New York? Our 50th-floor room had incredible Hudson River views. See if this hotel is worth the price for your next NBA trip.
title: Mandarin Oriental, New York Review

children.text: After our two nights at the
Park Hyatt New York
, we spent three nights at the Mandarin Oriental New York. After our first
MO stay in Miami

, we were excited about our stay in New York.  The MO NY has a great location, and great staff however a small room with non-blackout curtains, an uncomfortable bed at this price point, we would not stay here again.
Booked a “one more night” promo, which was no longer available closer to the check-in date; where the best available rate for the Hudson River Room was $1,495 per night.
The hotel opened in 2003 with 244 rooms across floors 35 - 54 of the Deutsche Bank Center.

Located in the Hacienda Business Park, Hyatt House is a residential-style hotel ideal for extended stay travelers to the San Francisco area. Our hotel features large suites with complimentary breakfast, free parking, and a pool and hot tub for relaxation. Our spacious one and two-bedroom suites are designed to create contemporary experiences with separate living and kitchen areas, and modern work spaces. Engaging social spaces to meet with friends or colleagues, meeting rooms, and a prime location all cater to today’s traveler. -
Hyatt

negatives: Outdated  furniture and fixtures
Thin walls. We could hear our neighbor's dog barking late at night.
Dogs are allowed (if you prefer hotels free of pets )
The hotel grounds can feel a little sketchy at night
positives: Full kitchen equipped with fridge, stove,  pots, pans, microwave, etc.
Dogs are allowed ( for dog owners )
Breakfast is provided
seoExcerpt: Planning a trip to Pleasanton? We stayed at Hyatt House Pleasanton and loved the full kitchen and pet-friendly policy. See if it fits your family trip.
title: Hyatt House Pleasanton Hotel Review

children.text: This is a good hotel as a last option. Nothing fancy about it but you will be ok if you are using it as a place to rest your head and leave all day.
After landing at Miami airport at 8 am, from our LAX red-eye, we retrieved our checked luggage, collected our rental car, then headed towards the Hyatt Regency Miami for our one-night stay.

We arrived at the hotel around 9 am & parked the rental off to the side of the large driveway. Upon walking in, I approached the front desk to ask if it was possible to check-in. They pointed to a sign stating it would be $50 for early check-in, to which I asked: "Even for a Hyatt Globalist?". They laughed & stated "No silly let's get you checked in".

After ID & credit card verification I was given keys to room 2016, a double on the 20th floor. They noted that there were no clean King rooms available as they had an event the day before & said to check later that afternoon for a possible room change.

We moved the car from the parking space to valet (complimentary on this booked award stay) & the bellhop helped take the luggage out of the car & into a cart. Then we were off into the elevator up to the 20th floor.

The room was spacious & functional, however, the decor was dark & drab. There was a balcony with views into Brickell, however, the balcony door seemed to have been intentionally altered to not be opened by patrons. The Chromecast-enabled TV was small, yet functional. My first impression was that the room was not the star of this hotel, its downtown Miami location was.

After taking photos & videos of the room, we closed the blinds & went to sleep, still a bit languid from the overnight flight. Upon awakening, we heard a not-so-faint hum coming through the walls. After waiting a few minutes, the sound did not disappear &

The Hyatt Regency Miami is located adjacent to the Miami Convention Center, this polished riverfront hotel is a 6-minute walk from Bayfront Park and 2.3 miles from the Vizcaya Museum & Gardens.

Low-key rooms offer free Wi-Fi, flat-screen TVs, and iPod docks. Club rooms have access to a lounge serving free continental breakfast and afternoon snacks. Suites add separate sitting areas.

negatives: Breakfast service was a hodgepodge & felt maniac. There were two people taking orders, however, they didn't communicate with each other so we had to repeat the order to the second person, noting we already ordered with the first person.
The hotel needs renovations as the furnishings are old. Not a fan of the hotel's bathroom that have shower curtains, and a petri dish for bacteria.
Booked a standard King room and received a [high floor] double.
positives: Good location in downtown Miami, close to shops, restaurants & Whole Foods.
Attentive & responsive front desk & valet staff.
Our first room (2016) had a weird humming noise in the walls, we asked to be moved to a different room & our 2nd room was spotless & humm-free.
The room was spacious, with a fridge & coffee pot, along with a work desk & chair.
seoExcerpt: Planning a trip to Hyatt Regency Miami? We loved the downtown location but had to switch rooms due to a wall hum. See our full review before you book!
title: Hyatt Regency Miami Review

children.text: This hotel is attached to the Miami Convention Center & can get very busy during conventions/events. Our stay was quiet with a few hiccups at breakfast & during checkout. I would stay here again for a few nights, noting the bed comfort was not to my liking & at the price point of 12,000 points for our one-night stay.
"Sleep is a necessity. Really good sleep is a luxury." -
Ameswell Hotel

negatives: On our 2nd visit the parking lot was no longer free.
positives: Good location in Silicon Valley, right off the highway.
Great restaurants with reasonable prices and tasty food. Had dinner at the Roger as well as breakfast and coffee at the Flyby.
Large gym with plenty of space & equipment. The gym has a floor to ceiling windows that let in lots of light.
seoExcerpt: Staying at The Ameswell Hotel in Mountain View? We loved the bright gym and tasty food at The Roger. Is it the best sleep in Silicon Valley? Read our take.
title: The Ameswell Hotel Review

children.text: "Desert sun, Vegas moments" - Las Vegas Hilton at Resorts World

negatives: During check-in, there was no mention of my gold status or elite benefits. Dorothy, the front desk attendant, was very new and kept going to the back office for answers to the questions I had.
I checked in 24 hours before and requested a digital key that never came. After check-in when I requested a digital key, the Hilton app kept giving an error message.
No in-room coffee machine. No complimentary coffee was provided.
The clock in our room was one hour behind (easily fixed). Does that mean the clock has been wrong since March 13, 2022, when Daylights Saving began?
The gym is open from 5am to 8pm. Which we found out when we tried to access at 11pm. Such a weird time for this massive resort located in a city full of nightlife.

There was no text feature (either with the hotel directly or via the Hilton app). We had to join the check-in line for simple inquiries, which sometimes resulted in a 15-minute wait to speak to someone.

The daily $45 resort fee includes (spoiler, nothing):
"Guest internet access; smart TV casting ability; 10% off spa or fitness retail; 5% off spa or fitness treatments; 5% off cabana experience; 5% off 2 pool chair experience; unlimited local and toll-free calls."
The hotel does not provide a complimentary airport shuttle service (which could be included in the daily $45 resort fee).

The Hilton app had limited functionality, unable to see bill charges. (You can view your room charges with the in-room television,  however, noted the charges listed were all coded as "sales tax" which was incorrect).
YouTube TV Chromecast functionality was not working (known YouTube API issue).
Vending machine on the floor was completely sold out. Mentioned to Dorothy at the front desk who stated it was through a third party & they did not have a way to refill it.
No robes or slippers were provided. I did not remember to ask when I went back down to the front desk.
The bathroom door only opened halfway.
positives: No line during check-in.
The bathroom was a nice size with nice amenities (hand soap smelled good).
The high floor, corner room was quiet.
AC worked well. Upon entering the room it was quite warm & we set it to 69 and the room was cool within 30 minutes.

The room key is programmed for your floor (both a pro and con). For security, if your room is on the 58th floor, you can only access the 58th floor with your key card. However, if you have family on multiple floors, you cannot access their floors that differ from yours.
Full-sized toiletries in the bathroom.
In-room fridge, separate from minibar to store personal food.
Both nightstands had multiple power outlets including USB charging capabilities.
The city view was nice from the 58th floor.
At 7 am on the day of check-out, I spoke with John at the front desk about a late check-out. Was given a 12 pm complimentary check-out and was informed that a 1 pm would cost $50.
seoExcerpt: Staying at Las Vegas Hilton at Resorts World in Las Vegas? We loved the quiet corner room and the great bathroom soap. See our full review of the stay.
title: Las Vegas Hilton at Resorts World Review

children.text: Booked a one-night stay in a King Deluxe City View at Las Vegas Hilton at Resorts World directly with Hilton for $233.56 ($161 room charge + $45 resort fee + $27.56 taxes). According to the rate, this rate was a 'resort exclusive' for 20% in savings.
Arriving after 11 pm, we stayed here as it would be easier to transfer to Conrad for our two-night stay, the following day.
In the future, for $200/night, I would rather stay at the Conrad, which has bigger standard rooms and more in-room amenities.

The Hyatt Centric Brickell Miami is located in a vibrant area near shops and nightlife, this stylish hotel in a high-rise building is 6 miles from South Beach, 7 miles from Miami Beach, and 9 miles from Miami International Airport.
Sleek rooms with contemporary decor feature free Wi-Fi, flat-screen TVs, and balconies; some offer views of Biscayne Bay. Corner suites add floor-to-ceiling window
s

We went to Kyu for my youngest sister's birthday. Located in Wynwood, the restaurant has a large inside dining area as well as several tables outside 4 under the building awning & more located in the street.

With our 615pm reservation, we were seated promptly outside at one of the four tables located right outside the main entrance. After being seated & greeted by our waitress, we asked if we could do the tasting menu due to our party's lactose intolerance. The waitress left to check with the kitchen & upon her return triumphantly announced we could indeed have the tasting menu.
The chef-tasting menu consists of 9 menu items listed as "Enjoy a delicious selection of Chef's favorite seasonal dishes, perfectly sized to your group. Let us do the hard work"

We had a few minutes before happy hour ended (at 630pm) and put in two orders of Old Fashioned (w/ George Dickle Rye) along with one Margarita with Olmeca Altos Plata Tequila. Each drink was $10 ($7 happy hour + $3 specialty upcharge).
We sipped on our drinks and chatted while we waited for the first dish to arrive.
1st course was Krunchy Kale ($9), which ranked 7th out of the 8 entrees for all of us. Overall this starter was okay & not something I would order again.
2nd course was Crispy Spicy Hamachi Tartare (21), which ranked 1st of the 8 entrees for my spouse & sister while ranking 2nd of the 8 entrees for me.

While I don't like meat tartare, I enjoy fish/seafood tartare. The crispy rice base was topped with wasabi mayo & the fish was the perfect mixture of crunchy, melty, sweet & spicy. I would definitely order this entree again.
3rd course was Roasted Cauliflower ($20), which ranked 5th and 6th for my spouse & sister respectively while ranking 4th for me.

Upon setting the entree down, we were instructed to cut up the cauliflower & mix it with the herb vinaigrette. The kitchen placed the goat cheese on the side, rather than underneath the cauliflower for our lactose intolerance, which we greatly appreciated. I loved this entree and would definitely order it again.

4th course was Crispy Pork Belly ($17, which ranked 5th for my sister & me while ranking 6th for my spouse. While the pork belly was nice & tender,  I personally did not like the bun. It was "mushy" and not as sweet as expected.
5th course was Thai Fried Rice Stone Pot w/ egg ($25), which ranked 3rd for my spouse & sister, while ranked 6th for me.

The entree came with table-side preparation, where the waiter mixed all the ingredients together & portioned it out in silver bowls. My spouse & sister thoroughly enjoyed this meal, however, the rice, to me, tasted like the burnt rice you find at the bottom of the pot & I felt it needed a bit more, something. I would be interested in trying this entree with the king crab option, to see if the crab provides that special something I was looking for.
The 6th course was Beef Short Ribs ($45), which ranked 2nd for my sister, 3rd for me & 4th for my spouse.

When the entree was set, we were instructed to squeeze the lime over the meat. The meat was tender, and the contrast of the sauce with the lime was delectable. The sweet soy and garlic soy were so good, my sister refused to wipe the sauce from her hands and saved it for the last lick. This was a flavorsome entree I will think about until my next trip to Kyu Miami.
The 7th course was Grilled Bok Choy ($11), which we all agreed ranked 8th of the entrees. I love bok choy, however, this entree needed to be cooked a bit longer as the stem was tough.
Less than a minute after the bok choy was placed on the table, the 8th course of Wagyu Beef Brisket ($49) arrived. This ranked 1st for me, 2nd for my spouse, and 4th for my sister.
The kitchen's instruction was to make lettuce wraps with the meat, sides, spices & sauces provided. The meat melted in your mouth & was a great "end" to the meal.
The 9th course was Tropical Fruits ($10) which was brought out with "Happy Birthday" written in chocolate on the plate, along with a candle.

seoExcerpt: We loved Din Tai Fung at the Aria Las Vegas. The pork chop fried rice was great, and the jasmine tea was the best I've ever had. Highly recommend a visit!
title: Din Tai Fung Restaurant Review

children.text: Din Tai Fung at the Aria in Las Vegas was a delicious dining experience. The food was incredible; we especially loved the Baby Back Ribs, Crab PK XLB, and Shrimp Spicy Wontons. The service was also top-notch, with attentive and courteous staff who made us feel well-cared for. The jasmine tea was the best I've ever had – the fact that they left the carafe at our table so we could enjoy hot tea throughout the meal was a lovely touch.

However, getting to the restaurant proved to be a bit of an adventure, as it's located on the casino floor, and we had to navigate through crowds and smoke to get there. We also had a slight hiccup with the hostess who told us there were no reservations available, but we were able to snag one online just 45 minutes later.

Finally, while the food was amazing, the portion sizes felt a bit small for the price. We also learned that ordering all our food at once meant it arrived in rapid succession, so next time, we'll space out our orders. Despite these minor points, we had an amazing evening at Din Tai Fung and would definitely return.

children.text: This place was a real find. We loved the generous portions, friendly staff, and convenient location close to our hotel and the beach. The prices were also very reasonable for the area. We enjoyed everything we ordered, especially the Chili Lime Wings, Fried Chicken, and Chicken & Honey Mustard Salad. The Lab Cadillac cocktail was a standout too, perfectly made with a delicious tajin rim.

While the service was generally good, it did slow down a bit during peak hours, which is understandable. Our only real disappointment was the Seafood Linguini. It was tasty, but we expected a heartier dish with more seafood, given the price. Overall, though, we had a great experience. This spot offers good food, good portions, great prices, and good service. We'll visit again on our next trip to Oceanside.

Our most anticipated stay of the year: 4 nights at Alila Ventana Big Sur. After flying into Oakland airport, we walked over to the Hertz counter to pick up our rental car. At the counter, the woman pointed us to a row of cars and told us to select one. After scanning the row of Hyundai Elantras, Nissan Altimas, and Toyotas we picked a 2021 Toyota Prius to take us on the 32-mile journey for our one-night stay at the Hyatt Centric Mountainview, further on the 120-mile journey to the Ventana Big Sur. After turning onto Coast Ridge Rd, we drove up to the front gate. We were greeted by an attendant who confirmed our reservation & then opened the gate for us to enter (when unattended there is a call box you can use to reach the front desk who can also open the gate). We drove up the windy, very small road to the valet station. The valet greeted us, reconfirmed our reservation & ushered us up the stairs to the Sur House for check-in. At check-in, we were provided a glass of wine & were given a map along with an overview of the property. Check-in was wonderful as we were one of two couples in the Social House. It was intimate and very informative. After check-in, we walked less than 1 minute to our Big Sur Villa, Room 23. This room is located in the building to the right of Social House, which made for a short walk to the pool & lawn seating areas.

The Big Sur Villa is "bi-level accommodation with plenty of room to roam". Downstairs there is an outdoor patio, a living room with a fireplace along with a dining area equipped with a Nespresso machine, a sink, ample storage & a mini-fridge. Upstairs there is a very comfortable King bed, two outdoor terraces along with a bathroom equipped with dual vanity, a soaker tub & a shower. At over 900 sq feet, the room was bigger than many NY apartments and was quite comfortable for our 4-night stay.

In the room was an Ipad, that could be used to order food (during our stay the hotel was all-inclusive), request housekeeping, or check your folio. Each night, we ordered in-room dining for breakfast the next morning, with the food arriving promptly at the scheduled time. After we were settled in the room, we headed out on the 0.5-mile walk to the Sur House for dinner. Prior to arrival, we received an email requesting our preferred dinner time & we selected 530pm. The walk from the room to the restaurant was through the Redwoods & absolutely breathtaking. There were chairs placed along the 0.5 walks if you needed to sit & the hotel also offered a service to help those unable to walk to the restaurant. Upon arrival, we were greeted, checked in & brought outside to the leftmost table facing the ocean. I would highly recommend coming to dinner early to ensure you can select this table which allows for endless views, as well as once the sun sets, the outdoor temperature rapidly drops. The staff has heat lamps by each table and will hand out blankets, however, the cold will still cut through you.

"With 59 secluded suites featuring expansive balconies, 160 magnificent acres of natural splendor on the rugged Pacific coast, and amenities and activities both private and purposeful, Ventana embodies the notion that space is luxury.
This is a place where everyone can find what they seek, from romance and emotional connection to perspective and solitary reflection."
Alila Ventana Big Sur

negatives: Internet was sporadic, not too big of a deal as we came here to explore the outdoors. Might be an issue if you come here planning on working remotely.
positives: Location, location, location: "Window" into Big Sur & its beauty. Close to Pfeiffer State Park & Pfeiffer Beach, with access to many other hiking trails. Great home base after exploring the outdoors.
Not usually a fan of the "log cabin" aesthetic, truly loved the room decor that paid homage to the surroundings in a clean and modern way.
Meal-inclusive package, where alcohol is not included. Note: this is a temporary perk, added due to COVID.
Nice room with a comfortable bed. Hooray for an in-room Nespresso & double sinks!

Wonderful staff. Everyone we interacted with was pleasant and super accommodating. From Michael & Richard during dinner service to Thomas & Ramiro during lunch. There are many ways to contact guest services, you can use the in-room tablet, use the in-room rotary phone, or text.

JW Marriott Marquis Miami

negatives: The walls are thin, can hear neighbors' TV, and people walking through the hallway.
The in-room fridge is a stocked mini-bar; there’s no place to store personal items.
No available tea kettle, so housekeeping brought hot water in carafes each time we wanted to make a cup of tea.
The room has visible wear and tear.
The bed was moderately comfortable, however, the pillowtop mattress cover kept sliding off & had to be reattached.
$25 (plus tax) destination fee
The property has a small pool.
A key card needs to be in the room slot to activate the lights
The mounted TV does not swivel making it hard to see from the seating area

The valet/parking situation is a hot mess. The parking space is limited, and can accommodate roughly 10 cars in two lanes. When cars are parked on the right-hand side, traffic moves at a snail's pace when folks are checking in and out.
The hotel has ongoing construction with scaffolding which deters from the hotel's outward appearance.
positives: Good location close to Brickell (across the bridge) and downtown Miami.
Great engaging staff, Mohammed at the front desk was very personable & provided an overview of the hotel at check-in.
Large bathroom with double vanity, soaker tub & shower. The water pressure was great & warmed up quickly.
Nice views of the bay (in between apartment complexes).
Large gym with plenty of equipment. There’s a gym studio with on-demand fitness classes.
In-room amenities included a robe and coffee machine. Requested 2nd robe and two pairs of slippers which were promptly delivered.
The hotel has an available text feature via the Marriott Bonvoy app allowing for easy communication.

boutique hotel, he said that while the JW was nice, it was not that nice and to taper my expectations by not comparing the two. Providing lush open spaces and light sea breezes, the Five-star hotel and spa offer an ideal location within walking distance of the finest shopping, dining, and nightlife experiences in Miami while providing the ultimate tranquil oasis for an escape. All guestrooms and suites come equipped with private balconies from which guests can enjoy stunning views of Biscayne Bay or Brickell Skyline. The hotel also boasts high-energy Food & Beverage concepts with breathtaking views and alfresco options." -
Mandarin Oriental Miami

negatives: Safe in the closet is at an awkward angle.
Wifi is slow (7 Mbps).

TV response time was slow. When you turned it on you would wait up to 30 seconds for it to register & then another 30 seconds for it to turn on
positives: Exceptional service. Across the board, everyone we encountered went above and beyond our expectations.
Great location in Brickell Key.
Spacious Junior Suite with comfy sofa & soaker tub.
Million dollar bay view.

Nice-sized gym with plenty of equipment.

Ample storage including a bath cart which housed additional towels.
Large lobby with floor-to-ceiling windows with expansive bay views.
In-room amenities included plush robes, comfy slippers that didn't disintegrate after 1 wear, and water was provided in glassware.
Great-tasting food (breakfast & dinner)

children.text: Book a stay through Mandarin Oriental's "One More Night" promotion, which offered a complimentary third night when you book three nights. Under their Fans of MO program our booking came with daily breakfast ($83), one time dining credit ($100) and a late check-out (1pm).

My friend spoke highly of the MO Miami for years and I was excited for our three night stay there. We had a wonderful time and now have a new bar for luxury hospitality. Excited for our upcoming stay at MO New York in the fall.

negatives: No in-room fridge for personal items, the fridge in the room is a stocked minibar
One robe in the room (requested a 2nd which was promptly delivered).
The bathroom was small, with one sink & a tub/shower combination that was difficult to get in and out of.
No water view and the room looks out at the nearby hotel pool.
In the room coffee machine did not go to sleep and flashed a light during the night.
The motion-activated light in the bathroom was unable to be turned off or dimmed. It was very bright & along with the flashing Illy night, which was very disruptive to the sleep cycle.
The pillows were soft & did not provide adequate support.
The room was outdated with visible wear & tear.
The bed was not comfortable, high partner motion transfer.
Windows are not soundproofed, could clearly hear music from cars on the street, 21 floors below.
The lounge was not frequently stocked. At noon it was out of coffee cups & guests were bringing cups from their rooms to use in the lounge.
positives: Early check-in (9 am) provided.
Good location in Brickell, close to Brickell City Centre & restaurants.
Upgraded to lounge access room (21st floor).
Key card activated elevator.
Gym, while small, is open 24 hours. Note you have to walk through the spa to access.
Fast wifi (100+ Mbps).
The front desk staff was nice during check-in.
The room was spacious and had a desk, chair & Illy coffee machine

children.text: Spent 40k points on a one-night stay during our two weeks in Miami. While the staff was attentive and courteous, the dated room made the stay feel more like a Holiday Inn than Marriott's luxurious JW brand. Rooms on the 7th floor are updated and bookable as an "Inspired" Guest Room. For 40k points or less than $250 a night, I would book a stay in the Inspired room instead.

negatives: No pool or spa is available at the hotel.
No robes or slippers were provided in the room (could be requested).
The bathroom design was not functional (no shower wall to prevent leaking, which resulted in a pool of water in the bathroom after each shower).
The hotel has 4 elevators to service 21 floors which resulted in frequent waiting. We were on the 5th floor and used the staircase instead.
positives: Great location: across the street from the Manhattan Bridge pedestrian path; less than half a mile to the Canal Street subway station.
Modern updated rooms, with great artwork. Concrete walls which might be a negative to some.
Courteous staff: Hotel has a texting system to which they were very responsive.
2nd-floor lounge area: great space with coffee & tea along with utensils & a microwave.
seoExcerpt: Staying at Hotel 50 Bowery in Manhattan? We loved the easy bridge access and responsive text service. See if the concrete walls fit your style here.
title: Hotel 50 Bowery Review

children.text: This was a
phenomenal
stay in a great hotel..
We had to downgrade our room as it was not available when we arrived at 9 am. The king-standard room was nice, definitely wished we had a couch to lounge on though.

The hotel is in the heart of Chinatown, with an amazing rooftop bar (The Crown). They allowed us to "visit" for a bit, however in order to order we needed a reservation which came with a $75 per person minimum.
For $101/night (plus taxes), this hotel was a great find & we will definitely return.

Such a hassle to figure out how to get from the airport to Waikiki. We looked at the Hawaii Tourism website along with watching some YouTube videos and made a reservation with Johnny Cab. As a backup, the hotel texted us that there were shuttle buses near the baggage claim that could take us to Waikiki. In the end, Jonny Cab worked perfectly and on our next visit we might just take "The Bus".
"Immerse yourself in the welcoming spirit of Aloha at Hyatt Centric Waikiki Beach. Ideally located in the heart of Waikiki, just off some of the
most beautiful beaches in the world
, and near countless island-inspired eateries and natural wonders, you’ll quickly discover this explorer’s paradise on O'ahu" -
Hyatt

negatives: Water filtration system & ice located on 1st, 7th, and 19th floor. Not an issue as our room was on the 19th floor.

Hotel restaurant is closed, as a Hyatt Globalist, I was given 500 points per night for the duration of our stay. This gave us time to try different local restaurants for breakfast each day. Hawaiian Aroma Cafe was a quick 5-minute walk & had a delicious acai bowl. Liliha Bakery located in the nearby Royal Hawaiin Center offered sit down service and delicious pastries. Heavenly, across the street, offered online ordering which helped save time from waiting in the line that always formed from 630 to 10 am.
Booked through Hyatt Privé however, there was no welcome amenity, and the $25 F&B credit was applied towards the room rate as the restaurant was closed.
This office building converted into a hotel 5 years ago offered no balconies.
Our room did not have a desk; hotel photos showed similar rooms with desks, however, they did not have a couch. If I had to choose between a couch and a desk, I will choose a couch.
Wifi was okay (Fast.com showed 9.1 Mbps), which worked for browsing however trying to stream Sling to the hotel TV was rather sluggish.
Small shallow pool
No onsite spa (guests were instructed to utilize the Hyatt Regency Spa instead)
YouTube TV Chromecast functionality was not working (known Hyatt/YouTube API issue)
positives: Good location in Waikiki. Close to many shops, restaurants, the beach & the bus stop is a block away. Ross is a few steps away with reasonably priced items, note the ling to checkout was extremely long when we went in on a Thursday afternoon.
Good views. The oceanview room has floor-to-ceiling windows which provided amazing views of the coastline.
Attached to Starbucks Reserve, can use mobile ordering to skip the line
$33 daily resort - while annoying, this resort fee adds value to our stay, including a Go-Pro rental.
The staff is very friendly, from the front desk agents to housekeepers to the valet, everyone greeted us.
While the gym is small it has adequate equipment: two treadmills, one Peloton, one elliptical, and free weights.
The bed was comfortable, it had 4 pillows that were different firmness.
The room was spacious with plenty of storage. I would see no issues with storing a week’s worth of clothes in the room.
The bathroom was spacious with double vanity & large shower.
The hotel has 4 elevators and there was rarely a wait. A keycard was needed to access guest room floors.
Comfortable, warm robes were provided
The hotel provided daily housekeeping, a rarity I thought was limited to luxury, 5-star hotel brands.
Very responsive text feature; The 10 pm in-app requests for slippers and kettle were promptly delivered.
