children.text: Booked under Hyatt Privé at $259/night. With great staff, great location, and modern spacious rooms, we would definitely stay here again.
Booked a "Deluxe King Room" DTLA Getaway Package for $189/night which came with a $50/nightly hotel credit. Checking the package on August 30th the nightly rate had increased to $294/night.
After flying into LAX airport, taking the LAX FlyAway bus to Union Station & then taking the number 28 bus (
which was free & I still don't know why

), we finally arrived at the JW Marriott LA Live. We waded past the LSU paraphernalia to get to the lobby check-in. Check-in was fast & prompt and we were given keys to room 1738, a Deluxe King City View room.
The hotel charges a $30/nightly destination fee that includes a
$20/night food & beverage credit,
2 tickets to the nearby Grammy Museum,
1 hour of bowling (& 2 rental shoes) at Lucky Bowling
Daily popcorn at the Regal Cinema (with popcorn voucher)
Daily yoga class
Daily wine tasting
Enhanced wifi (
same benefit for Gold members
After checking in & taking photos of the room, we ordered room service.
For our first meal, we spent $117, which was $87 for food & $31 in fees
Wagyu burger ($28)
Ceaser salad ($12)
Chicken wings ($16)
Pasta bolognese ($21)
Ginger Ales ($5)
Diet Coke ($5)
Hot water & 2 teacups ($0)
We were quoted a 30-minute wait time for our meal & it arrived in 20 minutes. All the food was delicious, my favorite was the pasta bolognese. I love fresh pasta & JW's Savoa restaurant is top-notch.
We ordered breakfast for our two mornings & both arrived promptly & were delicious.

This 17th-floor King room was very spacious & comfortable for our two-night stay. With great views of the Staples Center & LA convention center, the couch was a nice place to hang out after a day of exploring.
The TV allowed for YouTube streaming, and the bathroom shower had decent water pressure.

negatives: The bed was meh (rated 3/5), decent for 2 nights, but not as comfortable as other JW hotels.
The in-room coffee machine was subpar for the JW brand (Illy coffee stand in the lobby, Starbucks behind the hotel)
Small gym & small pool

$30 daily destination fee. While I appreciated the tickets to the Grammy Museum, not a fan of destination fees, especially since at check-in I was not informed about how to claim offers & had to come back downstairs to inquire & get the applicable vouchers.
The hotel did not notify us about hosting the LSU v UCLA game. The hotel was packed, causing lines to form, with little to no enforcement of the mask mandate (all staff were masked).
positives: Great location in downtown LA. Close to shops, restaurants, Staples Center & LA Convention Center.
Exceptional staff: fast response to requests, in-room dining arrived on time or earlier than quoted.
Great food: ordered dinner & breakfast & everything tasted great. Appreciated they offered in-room dining with plates & silverware.
Spacious room with a nice view (on the 17th floor)
seoExcerpt: Staying at JW Marriott Los Angeles L.A. Live? We loved the fast room service and prime spot near the arena. Read our honest review of the stay here.

children.text: We paid $517 ($189/night + $30 daily destination fee & taxes) for our two-night stay. Overall a nice stay in downtown LA would stay again if less than $200/night, and they are not hosting an event after COVID things settle down.

Featuring soundproof windows, modern rooms have free WiFi, flat-screen TVs, and coffeemakers. All offer work areas; suites (some with mini-fridges and microwaves) add separate sleeping and living space. In-room dining is available 24/7.

negatives: The bed was okay, the pillows were too soft.
TV started on the Windows screen & did not have Chromecast functionality.
Pricey for an airport hotel, range to upwards of $200 (plus taxes & fees) per night.
positives: Great location close to LAX airport
Nice staff, responsive to text message inquiries
Spacious room with table & couch. Double-paned windows (while dirty) kept most of the airport noise out.
Nice gym with runways views from the treadmill
room: 1 King Bed Runway View High Floor

@hyattregency_lax

. Booked a King Room & was upgraded to a King Runway View on the 8th floor. The hotel has 13 floors, with the Fitness Center & "city view" conference rooms on the 13th (Penthouse) floor. Overall we had a nice stay at the hotel & would stay here again if we had an early flight from LAX.

A towering icon within a vibrant Central Business District, Fairmont Austin is uniquely located in downtown Austin amid the greenery of Palm Park and Waller Creek. Our 37-story luxury hotel in Austin features 1,048 richly appointed guest rooms and suites with picturesque vistas of Austin's dramatic cityscape, Lady Bird Lake, and the State Capitol. At Fairmont Austin, indulge in premium amenities embodying all the finest qualities of a 4-star hotel in Austin. -
Fairmont Austin

lounge: yes, paid or member only access
negatives: Friday the alarm system was triggered on the 33th floor & the response was lackluster.
Room 3341 is across from the service elevator. Could hear loud noises as employees maneuvered through.
Room has visible wear & tear including ripped wallpaper & scuffed drawers & door frames.
Can hear street noise in the 33rd-floor room.
Bathroom did not have a rainfall or hand-held option.
Elevator key card can only be tapped on one side.
TV remote is slow to respond.
While the lounge food was good there were limited options. Saw same items for breakfast, canapes & dessert over the days.
Shower door didn't close all the way, resulting in water on the bathroom floor.
positives: Benjamin in the Gold Lounge is amazing. Very personable & helpful around the lounge.
Plush comfortable bed. Pillows were of varying firmness which allowed for a good night's sleep.
Spacious bathroom with water closet & large shower. Included Le Labo amenities (Rose 31)
Key card needed to access guest room floors.
Fairmont Gold room came with free premium wifi (23 Mbps)
Room has plenty of power outlets and USB charging (two per nightstand).
In room fridge is a paid mini fridge. Requested a fridge for personal items which was delivered promptly.
Large TV with Chromecast functionality which was easy to use.
Daily housekeeping & nightly turn down service.
Good selection of snacks & seating in the lounge, which was rarely at 25% occupancy the first two days. Next few days the lounge was busier. There was ample seating however it was not as quiet.
The hotel has 10 elevators divided into two sections allowing for fast access to higher floors.
Delicious freshly baked pastries in the lounge.
seoExcerpt: Staying at Fairmont Austin? We loved the Le Labo toiletries and Benjamin in the Gold Lounge. See why this was our favorite Texas stay for our NBA trip.

children.text: Upgrade to the Fairmont Gold room for a higher floor room with lounge access.

title: Fairmont Austin Texas

children.text: Nice hotel for a few days while attending a conference. Close to Austin Convention Center with plenty of shopping & restaurants nearby. Austin is a very walkable city & this is a great base hotel. We would likely only return if we needed to be in close proximity to the convention center. Will look for other hotels in Austin for our next stay.
Opposite Bankers Life Fieldhouse arena, this informal hotel is a 7-minute walk from Indianapolis Union railway station, 2 miles from Indianapolis Zoo and a mile from White River State Park. -
Hyatt House Indianapolis/Downtown

negatives: A half bottle of Dr Pepper was in the fridge when we checked in, a cleanliness issue.
There were several homeless folks in the park near the transit center & police station on the walk to Whole Foods, a possible safety issue.
Street noise can be heard from the 6th floor room, might be bothersome to some especially when events are happening.
Valet parking is $43 per night.
Shower water pressure is low & Internet is slow (9 mbps).
3 days after checking out the stay had not posted to my Hyatt account & needed to be manually requested.
positives: Great location close to Gainbridge Fieldhouse.
Studio room is spacious with large spacious bathroom.
The hotel has a large gym along with coin-operated laundry with 2 washers & 2 dryers.
Staff is friendly & complimentary breakfast is available.
The hotel has 4 elevators that work efficiently. After the Fever game, there was a line & a bit of wait, which is to be expected.
Hotel has a [small above-ground indoor] pool.
room: Studio Kitchen Suite | King Bed (plus sofa bed) | Room 606
seoExcerpt: Staying at Hyatt House Indianapolis? We loved the huge gym and proximity to Gainbridge Fieldhouse. See our full review of this budget-friendly hotel here.
title: Hyatt House Indianapolis/Downtown Hotel Review

children.text: We were in town for a Fever WNBA game & the Hyatt House is located directly across the street, which is a huge plus. We paid $380 for our 2-night stay, and with a spacious studio wth a kitchenette, this is a great base to attend an event at Gainbridge. If doing other activities outside the area, I would stay somewhere else.

negatives: Thin "walls": could hear the upstairs neighbor walking around, but didn't hear neighbors on our floor.
New hotel yet the bathroom hot water faucet "popped" out & was difficult to turn off.
Confusing light switches spent a few minutes trying to identify what turned on/off.
Windows don't open, the room was "warm" overnight.
positives: Great location: walking distance to Target, Trader Joe's, Walmart & Whole Foods
"Stylish" new hotel, spacious standard room floor plan.
Soft, comfortable bed
Free self-parking ($25 valet)
In-room Keurig with Dark Magic pods (my favorite)
seoExcerpt: Staying at Hyatt Centric Mountain View? We loved the walkable location near Target and the comfy beds. See our full review before your next road trip!
title: Hyatt Centric Mountain View Review

children.text: Nice new (opened in 2019) hotel in a great location filled with shops & restaurants. Although the hotel has been open for a while, they still seemed to be working out the kinks.

For the price we paid of $109.24 (total) for our one-night stay, we would definitely stay here again, asking for a higher floor room. During summer this hotel costs upwards of $400/night (+tax) which definitely isn't worth it.

The Hotel Beaux Arts hotel is located in a glass and steel high-rise, this stylish hotel is a 10-minute walk from Bayfront Park and an 8-minute drive from American Airlines Arena.

Minimalist rooms and 1-bedroom suites offer ocean or bay views, as well as marble bathrooms, flat-screen TVs, and iPads. All also have free Wi-Fi and coffeemakers.

negatives: Weird check-in, this hotel is on the top 3 floors of the JW Miami Marquis & you need a key card to get to the 39th floor to check in. The JW front desk checked us in (after walking to the elevator & walking out after realizing we needed a key card).
Unlike Hyatt which doesn't charge resort fees on award bookings, I had to pay a $25 resort fee for services I never used.

Also unlike Hyatt where I don't pay for parking, valet parking here was $55 for the night. The attendant who helped us was not very attentive as they were on the phone (& stayed on the phone) when we pulled up. We read reviews that it takes about 30 minutes for the valet to get the car, so we requested it 30 minutes before we needed it & headed downstairs when they said it was ready. The entrance/valet is super small & gets a bit congested.
positives: Stylish room with great views & comfortable bed.
Large bathroom with spray jet bathtub
Plush bathrobes (& slippers)! So comfortable I considered buying them (but didn't since the suitcase had minimal space left).
Illy in-room coffee machine.
The front desk staff was nice & responsive.
seoExcerpt: Staying at Hotel Beaux Arts in Miami? We loved the spray jet tub and plush robes. See if this high-rise is worth it for your next NBA arena road trip.
title: Hotel Beaux Arts Review

children.text: Located on the top floors of the JW Marquis Miami, after living in South Florida for 7 years, finally got an opportunity to visit this hotel.
Used 40k points to book a Rockwell room & were upgraded to the O'Keefe. Nicely appointed room, with large bathroom with double vanity, soaker tub & shower.
Great use of 40k Marriott Bonvoy points, although I was still charged the resort & parking fee. Despite the awkward front desk situation, would definitely stay here again.
After one night at the
Manchester Grand Hyatt San Diego
, we walked the 0.9 miles to the Andaz San Deigo, a 159-room boutique hotel located in Gaslamp Quarter.

We used a Hyatt Free Night to book a standard Queen room & were not provided a Globalist upgrade at check-in. Thomas at the front desk checked us in & provided us with a (plastic) glass of wine & beer. As a King room was not available when I made the reservation, I asked Thomas if a King room was available at check-in. He said to call down to the front desk in 90 minutes & check. (When I called down, they said no King rooms were available).

We took the elevator up to the 5th floor to our room for the night, #507. While were appreciated having a room far from the elevator, the room did not have good views. Also noticed earplugs in the room, which was a bit concerning, however, outside noise was not an issue & I got a great night's sleep.

After placing our bags in the built-in closet, we took photos & recorded room tour videos. After we decided to make a cup of coffee with the in-room Keurig & upon opening noticed the machine had not been cleaned since it was placed in the room. So before using, we did a deep clean with some Lysol wipes & did a few hot water rinses.

negatives: The room faced the Salvation Army & there was trash & homeless people on the street.
The Keurig had not been cleaned in a while: we did a full wipe down & several hot water rinses.
We noticed earplugs in the room, noting there may be some street noise.
positives: While the room is small, the space is functional & cozy.
Comfy bed with firm pillows. We got a great night's sleep on the Queen bed.
Delicious breakfast a the Rooftop at STK.
seoExcerpt: Staying at the Andaz San Diego? Our review covers the cozy rooms and that tasty breakfast at STK. See if it’s worth it for your next NBA arena trip here.
title: Andaz San Diego Review

children.text: Used a Hyatt Free Night to stay at the Andaz San Diego which is a nice hotel in San Diego's Gaslamp Quarter. While the queen room was small, it was quite functional & used the space well. Would definitely stay here again for the comfy bed & delicious breakfasts.

"Nestled next to the legendary Beringer Estate Winery, and just a short walk from St. Helena’s vibrant downtown Main Street, Alila Napa Valley is ideally placed to experience the best of California’s most celebrated wine region – from exploring its beautiful countryside to indulging in its epicurean lifestyle" -
Alila Napa Valley

negatives: GPS had an issue finding the entrance, the hotel sign is small and hard to see from the road. We drove past the entrance & GPS took us on a 5-minute turnaround.
There seemed to be confusion regarding what is covered under the $55 resort fee.
There was not any security on the property. At Ventana, you had to use your key card to access the entrance to the property when on foot. Those driving in had to check in with a gate agent.
positives: Spacious room, with a large shower and tub. Separate toilet (with bidet) with a second vanity.
Excellent, attentive, friendly staff. The hotel offers a text option & was very responsive to our inquiries.
Fast, reliable wifi (91 MBPS)
Great location in St. Helena, close to Beringer winery, less than 0.5 miles to downtown.
The bed was comfortable, but the pillows were not as firm as I prefer.
Automated light switches & black-out curtains.
Decent size a gym, with three treadmills, two Peloton bikes, a row machine & free weights.
In-room Nespresso machine & kettle.
The room has a large private balcony with a fire pit and ample seating. Spent ample time in the rocking chairs on the balcony.
Delicious food from on-property Acacia House
Even though I declined housekeeping during app check-in, our room was serviced daily and there was nightly turn-down service.
Quiet resort, offering a unique experience being on the Beringer vineyard.
Awesome views. Our room was in the center of the floor's 5 rooms which allowed for complete vineyard views.
room: King Bed Vineyard View High Floor with Balcony | Room #232
seoExcerpt: Stayed at Alila Napa Valley in St Helena. Loved the huge shower and fast wifi. See our full review of this wine country spot before your next trip.
title: Alila Napa Valley Hotel Review

children.text: For our wedding anniversary, we used a free night award and 30,000 points for a two-night stay at Alila Napa Valley, where rates were $1,292 per night.

After staying at Ventana Big Sur, we were excited to visit our 2nd US Alila property. With great staff, great food, great views, and a great location this was definitely a trip to remember. We would love to stay here again!
Tip: The rooms are numbered as such: building, floor number, room. So our room 232 was in building 2, on the third floor.

"Steps away from destination-worthy dining, Cherry Creek's premier shopping, and outdoor trails, our luxury Denver hotel is your place in the heart of it all. Our sophisticated, well-appointed suites, featuring elegant five-piece marble bathrooms, double closets, and pillow-top mattresses, embody the luxury of JW Marriott. From inspired culinary offerings, inviting shared areas, refined meeting spaces, and Rocky Mountain views, we provide everything you need and nothing that you don’t."
JW Marriott Denver Cherry Creek

negatives: No onsite pool
Due to lobby construction (slated to end Feb 2022), you have to walk through Toro restaurant to get to the temporary 2nd-floor lobby.
positives: Good location in Cherry Creek, close to indoor mall & Whole Foods.
Large gym with plenty of equipment.
Comfortable bed.
Spacious room with large bathroom.
In-room Nespresso machine.
Full-size toiletries, including hand soap.
Great staff, app requests were answered promptly. In-person interactions were friendly.
Valet was top-notch, even with the construction, the attendant communicated effectively & ensure everyone knew where to go.
Open 2nd-floor lounge, with a coffee machine & complimentary snacks.
For New Year’s staff put a bottle of champagne in the room with wine glasses.
Hand sanitizers located in multiple locations on each floor; disposable masks also available.
room: Mountain View King Guest Room | Room 621
seoExcerpt: Planning a trip to Denver? We stayed at the JW Marriott Denver Cherry Creek. Loved the huge gym and comfy beds. See if it fits your next NBA arena trip.
title: JW Marriott Denver Cherry Creek Review

children.text: We used two 35k certificates for our two night
#NYE
stay, where rates were upwards of $400/night. With no resort fee, a great location and exceptional staff I would definitely stay here again.

JW Houston Downtown

Designed for Social Discoverers, Renaissance Atlanta Airport Gateway Hotel showcases urban sophistication, modern style and first class service. Our Atlanta Airport hotel is located at the Gateway Center Arena, just 2 minutes from Hartsfield-Jackson International Airport via the 24-hour ATL SkyTrain free airport transportation train.  -
Marriott

lounge: yes, paid or member only access
negatives: Walls are thin, you can hear everything in the hallways & we could clearly hear the TV of the person in the connecting room.

We arrived close to midnight & the check-in gentleman, while polite & jovial, was doing the bare minimum. He told us incorrect information about the package we purchased & only went to ask someone else for confirmation after I asked follow up questions. He did not tell us where the gym was, how to access the wifi, or the restaurant hours. It was "welcome & here are your keys".

We were charged $45 for parking however we did not have a car. We surmise the parking check box was left on in our folio during check-in. We alerted the hotel to the error on day 2 and they removed the charges, however on day 3 we were charged $45 again.

We booked a rate with $25 F&B credit. When we checked-in the sole restaurant available for the credit was closed. Even after speaking with several different front desk agents over the course of 3 days about how to use our 1st day credit, we were unable to use.
Being an airport hotel, there were not that many (good) restaurants within walking distance.
The curtains in our room had stains on them & the curtains do not overlap enough to keep out the morning sun. I used a hanger to keep them closed.
View is of the parking lot and there is a train that comes through once a day that is quite loud.
No key card needed to access or move the elevator. The "5" floor button was rubbed off in the one (of two) elevator that seemed to be working.
The innerspring mattress had a sink in it & I had to rotate the mattress to get a good night's sleep. The 4 pillows provided were all  the same & the too soft.
The Marriott Titanium lounge is small & does not open on the weekends.
positives: The hotel was built in 2017 and is still in good condition considering the high transient occupation.
The room is spacious with a desk, a seating area & a small armchair with laptop tray.
Free access to the airport via the nearby sky train.
Premium wifi, once connected, was fast. Was able to have several Zoom meetings in the room with no issues.
SmartTV worked ok, the remote was sluggish & it frequently & randomly would sign out of YouTube.
The room had ample outlets.
The AC unit worked well & the room was cold.
The hotel has ample seating in the lobby. The ambiance is very modern & we liked the overall aesthics.
seoExcerpt: Staying at Renaissance Atlanta Airport Gateway Hotel in College Park? We loved the easy sky train access. See our full review of this clean, spacious spot.
title: Renaissance Atlanta Airport Gateway Hotel Review

children.text: Renaissance Atlanta airport is a great overnight base if you are going to a Dream WNBA game or need a room close to the airport.

Stay in the heart of downtown near all the excitement that makes Miami a global destination. The city’s best dining, nightlife, arts and entertainment are steps away from your unobstructed waterfront views.
Here

negatives: Small (width-wise) wrap around balcony with no seating available.
Two of the three bedrooms do not come with a TV.
Small drive-way, have to park on the street for access to hotel.
$50 parking per night (in & out allowed).

$45 daily amenity fee which includes: Fitness/Yoga classes, in-room Wi-Fi connection, local and 1-800 phone calls, 24-hour Concierge and Front Desk services, two refillable PATH water bottles, and two complimentary drinks upon arrival.
The room only had 3 robes (1 per bedroom) rather than per person. We requested 3 more robes & they were brought up.
Text communication was inconsistent. Sometimes they would answer immediately, other times it took several hours.
The couch in the unit was not large enough to accommodate our party of 6. Some folks sat on the floor.
The kitchen table came with 5 chairs. We asked for another chair to accommodate our party of 6 & were told they were unable to add furniture to our room.
positives: Great location in downtown Miami. Close to Bayside, Port of Miami & Kaseya Center. Great post-cruise location as well as easy walk to after a Miami Heat game.
Apartment style full service hotel with up to 3-bedrooms to accomodate 6 people.
Quiet hotel (with sound-proofed windows) with nice views.
Large two-level gym with lots of equipment (treadmill, smith machine, free weights)
Fast wifi (220 mbps). There were two ways to connect (room number & last name or with access code)
A washer & dryer is available in the unit; laundry pods were provided & replenished daily.
Nice wrap-around pool with a large TV showing professional sports games. Staff set up our chairs & brought around towels. We did not order food from the pool restaurant.
seoExcerpt: Staying at The Elser Hotel in Miami? We loved the sound-proofed windows and walking to Kaseya Center. See why it’s our top pick for a Heat game trip.
title: The Elser Hotel Review

children.text: We were looking for a downtown Miami hotel that could accommodate 6 people. Stumbled upon the Elser & booked directly with their 30% off 4-night promo. At $600/night our 3-bedroom suite was what we needed for our post-cruise family holiday. The hotel, while allowing 6 occupants, missed out on full points by simply ensuring there were enough amenities for all occupants. Overall a good stay & would recommend it for large groups.
'There’s nothing in the world like Las Vegas—and there’s absolutely nothing in Las Vegas like Wynn." -
Encore

negatives: No keycard activated elevator (you tap a keycard stand in front of an attendant before heading to the elevator.)
The large hotel doesn't feel personalized.
$45 resort fee no inclusions (basic wifi included).
The TV was glitchy & would stop working randomly.
No in-room coffee amenities or slippers were provided.
Not enough power outlets for all devices.
Visible dust on the minibar, and desk legs.
The four pillows on the bed were flat.
Our room was near a mechanical element and we heard incessant whirring through the walls during the entirety of our stay.
The ice machine on our floor did not work.
The gym was small for the size of the hotel.

The $100 credit received by booking through a travel agent was only usable at the spa, where treatments started at $150. While other hotels allow this credit to be used at food and beverage establishments in the hotel, Wynn seemed to "offer" a credit they know would go unused.
positives: Large (745 sq ft) spacious room with separate seating area
Large bathroom with dual vanity, shower, soaker tub & bath scale.
Firm, comfortable bed.
In-room Alexa controlled the lights & shades.
Breakfast at Espresso was reasonably priced & tastes great. The staff at Espresso was very nice.
Was provided complimentary 2 pm check-out.

We stood in line for 23 minutes and when we got to the front desk we realized we were in line for the Wynn side, rather than the Encore side. Crystie, the front desk agent, was very helpful & knowledgeable. Rather than send us to the Encore side to check in, she checked us in.
Can check in/check out via the kiosk located in the hotel lobby.
seoExcerpt: Staying at Encore at Wynn in Las Vegas? Our review covers the massive 745 sq ft room and comfy bed. See if this hotel is worth your family's next trip.
title: Encore at Wynn Review

children.text: Booked a one-night stay in an Encore Resort King (nightly rate of $220 + taxes & fees) through a travel agent (Virtuoso) and got upgraded to Encore Panoramic King (nightly rate $263 + taxes & fees).  Coming from the Four Seasons where I felt taken care of, the Encore at Wynn just feels like another Las Vegas strip hotel that didn't provide more than a spacious room with a view.

"In the CityCenter complex and a block from the Strip, this upscale, gaming-free all-suite hotel is connected via an outdoor walkway to Aria Las Vegas. Upscale suites have free Wi-Fi and flat-screen TVs, plus soaking tubs, kitchenettes, and living and dining areas. Upgraded suites add full kitchens, washers/dryers, and/or additional bedrooms and bathrooms. Some have views of the Strip or the Bellagio Hotel fountain". -
Vdara Hotel & Spa

negatives: Gym was small & the hours were limited (8am - 5pm).
The pool was closed and we were instructed to use the Aria pool. The walk between the hotels was 50% uncovered (unless you walked through the casino) & took around 5 minutes.

$45 daily resort fee "includes" wired and wireless internet, in-room local and toll-free telephone calls, access to 2,000 electronic newspapers, and airline boarding pass printing in the business center.

Note: As MGM Gold this is waived at all MGM properties.
The hotel does not have a "restaurant". The lobby Starbucks had limited hours, and the 24-hour Market Cafe didn't have an extensive menu. Most days we ate off-strip or at a restaurant in Aria.
The in-room tablet did not allow for pre-ordering breakfast the night before. You had to order during business hours.

Valet parking is $30/day Monday - Thursday and $35/day Friday through Sunday.

Note: Valet parking is complimentary for MGM Gold members.

MGM Rewards changed on February 1st. Our Feb 8th stay was met with confusion from staff regarding the perks (_free parking, waived resort fee,$100 credit, complimentary upgrade_).

Note: I emailed customer service on day 3 of our stay & Meghan contacted me to provide a resolution.
positives: Wifi was great (52 Mbps), and there were no issues with Zoom meetings.
Suites are equipped with a stacked washer & dryer, along with an electric stovetop, dishwasher, microwave, full fridge & freezer.
Complimentary laundry detergent and dryer sheets were available by contacting housekeeping.
Staff adhered to and enforced the indoor mask mandate.
There were hand sanitizer and mask stations throughout the hotel.
The valet was efficient, it never took more than 5 minutes to get our car, even during busy times.
Housekeeping was friendly and thorough.
Beautiful unobstructed views, able to see the Bellagio Fountain show along with the Nevada mountains.
Reid, the bellhop who brought our luggage, was nice. He provided tips & tricks about the room (how to control the light shade, who to call to request silverware & etc.)
Non-casino hotel (a negative for some). Patrons can visit the adjacent Aria hotel which has a casino.
Good mid-strip location. Easy access to nearby Cosmopolitan, nearby restaurants, and activities.
seoExcerpt: Staying at Vdara in Las Vegas? Our review covers the 52 Mbps wifi and full kitchen setup. See if this suite works for your next NBA arena trip here.
title: Vdara One Bedroom Penthouse Suite Hotel Review

children.text: After a 2-night stay in the Vdara Fountain Suite, we were offered a complimentary upgrade to a 56th floor One Bedroom Penthouse Fountain View Suite.

As an MGM Gold member, the $45 daily resort fee and $35 daily valet parking are waived. Booked under an MGM 30% deal and the Vdara Fountain View Suite costs $195 a night (total), which is pricey for a non-weekend stay in Vegas. For our dates, the Penthouse Fountain View Suite was listed for $349/night (plus taxes and fees).
If you are looking for a central Strip, non-casino hotel and you don't have a car, this is an option.
For almost $200/night, I would rather stay at the
Four Seasons Las Vegas
, another non-casino hotel located on the Strip, for better consistent service & amenities.

Grand Hyatt San Francisco welcomes you with a sophisticated elegance and refined modern style. Located in the heart of the city at Union Square, immerse yourself in the premier shopping, world-class dining, and nightlife of downtown San Francisco. Then retreat to your room where you can unwind and enjoy the spectacular views of the city by the bay -
Hyatt

lounge: yes, paid or member only access
negatives: AC unit was weird to figure out. Upon arrival we turned it off & opted to open the sliding glass door. After a few hours, we closed the sliding glass door & turned on the AC but the room was not getting any cooler. We turned the unit down to 65 F before the room started to feel comfortable.
Lounge is open during certain hours, outside of those hours it is locked. Would appreciate key-card access so folks can get coffee/water when needed.
The in-room desk chair is too low for the desk provided.
No suite upgrade, although there were suites available for booking.
$35 daily resort fee (waived for Globalist), inclusions are listed here: https://www.hyatt.com/en-US/hotel/california/grand-hyatt-san-francisco/sfous/policies. Spoiler: nothing of value.
Elevators did not require a key card to access the rooms, a security concern.
positives: Good location close to Market Street. Quick 5 minute walk to Powell station with access to Muni.
Grand Lounge staff was very personable & kept lounge stocked & clean.
Painless check-in, was able to get into room around 9 am.
Nice view of the Bay.
Wifi was easy to use, although it was not password protected. Was able to participate in Zoom calls with no issues.
TV had streaming functionality, which was quick to set-up.
seoExcerpt: Planning an NBA trip to San Francisco? We loved the Grand Hyatt's location near Powell station and early 9 am check-in. See our full review before booking!

children.text: Great hotel if you plan to visit the Chase Center
• 13 mins via Bus
• 21 mins via Tram
• 20 mins via Muni (free with an NBA Game ticket)

title: Grand Hyatt San Francisco Hotel Review

children.text: We were looking for a place to stay overnight in San Fran for less than $300. Our normal hotels were almost $500 and after some searching, we stumbled upon the Grand Hyatt San Fran which was priced at $275 (sans taxes).

With a location close to Market & Union, close to several train stations, shops and restaurants, it is a good home base for a few days. While the rooms are not too special, the front desk and Grand Lounge staff is very personable which makes it a great pick. While a good stay, I will test out other hotels in the area before returning to the Grand Hyatt.
NoMad Las Vegas
combines the grandeur of European casino hotels with the glamour and fun of our new home on The Strip at Park MGM. Book a room. -
Nomad

negatives: $42 daily resort fee that includes nothing: "In-room wireless internet access; unlimited local, domestic long distance (the 50 United States and DC) and toll-free calls; airline boarding pass printing; digital newspaper and magazine downloads through PressReader for duration of reservation; access to Paramount+ with SHOWTIME On Demand via in-room television; and fitness center access for guests 18+. Amenities, such as fitness center access, are subject to availability and guest demand."
TV remote was not working.
Wifi is horrendous, speed & connection drops frequently, evident while listening to a podcast that would stop intermittently. Speed test ranged from 2 mbps to 18 mbps.
positives: The room was ready at 13:30, greatly appreciated the early complimentary check-in.
In the middle of the strip, close to T-Mobile & Allegiant Stadium & many shops & restaurants.
Fast, efficient service. We asked for two extra pillows & a blanket during check-in & they were delivered promptly with a smile.
Great value, the room was listed for $119 per night plus $42 resort fee during a Tuesday check-in after Labor Day.
The room had plenty of amenities including a Nespresso machine, free water (a rarity in Las Vegas), robes, slippers, and a cloth laundry bag.
Keycard needed to access elevators, which is a great for a sense of security.
Overall liked the decor more than the sister property, Park MGM. Nomad is a good luxury option close to strip central at a lower price tag than compared to the Four Seasons or Waldorf Astoria.
seoExcerpt: Staying at NoMad Las Vegas? We loved the early 1:30 PM check-in and prime Strip location near the arenas. Read our honest review before you book your stay.
title: Nomad Las Vegas Hotel Review

children.text: A Stylish Stay with Connectivity Concerns

The Nomad Las Vegas offers a luxurious experience in a prime location with commendable service and a reasonable price point. The early check-in, prompt room service, and abundance of amenities enhance the overall experience. However, the hefty resort fee with lackluster inclusions, coupled with the unreliable Wi-Fi, detract from the overall value.
Recommendation:

Despite the drawbacks, the Nomad Las Vegas presents a compelling option for those seeking a stylish and convenient stay on the Strip. However, guests should be aware of the resort fee and potential Wi-Fi issues.

After spending one night at the Chicago Athletic Association, we hopped on the 147 bus for a quick 20-minute ride to spend our second Chicago night at the Thompson Hotel. At our stop, we got off the bus & started the 0.3-mile walk to the hotel.
Note

: Each time (of the three times) we navigated to this hotel, we got lost. Our GPS had issues with the area & we ended up walking further than necessary to get back to the hotel. Silver lining: I hit my 10k step goal on both days.
This hotel is in a "posh" part of town: close to the Waldorf Astoria & Ritz Carlton hotels, surrounded by high-end shopping with the likes of Prada, Dior & Gucci.

Upon arrival (around 2 pm) we were greeted by several bellmen, who were the highlight of the stay. We entered the hotel & checked in & were notified that we had been upgraded from a King Room to a King Corner (on the 18th floor).
We hopped in the elevator, stepped off on the 18th floor, took a left & making a beeline for the corner room.

Upon entering the room, we noted it was almost twice the size of the Chicago Athletic, with floor-to-ceiling windows encompassing two walls. If only we had requested a water view room, the views would have been even better,
not diminishing the expansiveness of our view.
The view was so amazing, we neglected to check out the bathroom, which was gigantic with a large soaker tub and a separate shower.

While the Chicago Athletic had double sinks I would definitely trade that for the full soaker tub, any day. (Side note: ran to Target & grabbed some Epsom salt & had two baths during our one-night stay here.)

On the downside, the in-room fridge was locked so basically unusable and not sure what was up with the TV, however the picture was sporadically grainy or frozen. While not a huge deal as we were not in the room to watch TV, still something that should be fixed.
TV Issue
We dropped off our stuff in the room & headed back downstairs to grab a late lunch at the nearby Velvet Taco.
After eating we came back to the room to change before heading back to Grant Park for the 1830 Music Festival (
which was amazing
The hotel did not offer breakfast, as the attached restaurant Nico was only open for dinner. After waking up at 7 am, I ordered pickup from the nearby Wildberry Pancakes & Cafe.

Ventured out in the cool & quiet early morning for the quick 0.5-mile walk to the restaurant (located next to the Ritz Carlton) & was astonished that before 8 am the restaurant was packed, with people standing outside, waiting. On the way back to the room, stopped at the stand located outside the hotel & grabbed coffee, a muffin, and a fruit smoothie to accompany the brisket hash & chicken and biscuits.
With a 4 pm check-out, lounged in the room for the remainder of the day before heading to the airport.

negatives: No available in-room fridge locked wine fridge.
No in-room coffee maker; no coffee is available in the lobby.
TV consistently cut in & out, staticky images: no Chromecast option.
No ice machine available (requested & was given a container of ice)
positives: Great location in the Gold Coast, with tons of high-end shops & restaurants within walking distance. Away from the touristy part of town.
Wonderful staff, especially the doormen who were always chatting with us & helping us find our way.
Great views, definitely try for an odd-numbered room for a lake view.
Large gym with peloton bikes. (Note: view from treadmills was of a parking garage.)
Spacious bathroom with shower & large tub.
Stumbled upon the Secret Stairwell - an art gallery of local artists.

children.text: Our stay at this hotel was largely enjoyable, with highlights including the stunning coastline views from our comfortable room, the convenient Chromecast TV feature, and the fun we had exploring the area with the included e-bikes. Safe issue:

Reached out to the front desk who sent up an engineer who after 3 attempts was unable to open it. He left saying he would return however 60 minutes later, nothing. After contacting the front desk, the engineer called back to say they would return in the morning. The next morning after 30 minutes of drilling the safe was opened.

Our downtown Denver boutique hotel welcomes locals and globetrotters alike to indulge in the best the Mile High City offers. Located in the heart of vibrant LoDo — the city’s historic Lower Downtown neighborhood and near the RiNo District, Thompson Denver is an easy walk to historic Union Station, Larimer Square, and the buzzy bars and restaurants of the Dairy Block. Inside our luxury hotel, find sophisticated meeting facilities and event venues, celebrated French cuisine at Chez Maggy, and creative cocktails at our 6th-floor lounge featuring stunning views of the city and mountains beyond. negatives: $21.06 destination fee inclusions listed here: https://www.hyatt.com/thompson-hotels/denth-thompson-denver/policies

The hotel is within walking distance of the King of Prussia Mall, the Valley Forge National Historical Park, and many other popular attractions. Hyatt House Philadelphia/King Of Prussia offers a variety of amenities, including free Wi-Fi, a fitness center, an indoor pool, and a complimentary breakfast buffet. children.text: Overlooking the Atlantic Ocean, the Confidante Miami Beach hotel is set in a1940s art deco skyscraper. It's a 2-minute walk from Miami Beach. Chic rooms with a 1950s vibe feature minibars and flat-screen TVs. Suites add sitting areas, living rooms, and/or kitchens with wet bars and fridges. negatives: Ambersweet restaurant was closed during our Monday to Wednesday stay. All food ordered was taken to-go.
The hotel charged a 20% service fee on every order. This 20% charge was not taken off for Globalist breakfast orders.
At 350 square feet, the room & bathroom was small. I intentionally booked the King Deluxe to have a sofa & the "upgraded" room did not have a sofa.
Wished the hotel had a more authentic Miami menu, including Peruvian, Cuban, or Venezuelan food.
positives: Great location on Miami Beach with direct access to the beach.
Booked through Hyatt Privé which came with roundtrip transportation from Miami airport. They picked us up from the Hyatt Centric Brickell & dropped us off at Miami airport.
Great staff: from check-in to the bartender and restaurant staff, everyone we encountered was nice & professional.
The hotel has a Museum of Graffiti collection, with an available audio tour, which was nice during a rainy day at the hotel.
Room decor definitely has beachy vibes with carpet & furniture. Outdoor furniture was bright yellow & blue, which simulated the sun & ocean.
Oceanfront views were a show-stopper. Spent most of the time on the balcony on the lounge chairs.
Two pools (albeit next to each other), one for families & one for adults.

After living & working in South Florida for almost 10 years, I have come to tolerate Miami's lackluster customer service & premium proximity prices. I was surprised as the staff was pleasant and the hotel felt well-maintained; I would stay here again.

Barn door bathroom (sans lock).

They say don't judge a book by its cover, and I judge hotel rooms by their (sometimes, lack of) coffee machine. The Nespresso in this double queen gets high marks, along with the double-walled Bodum glasses.
Redeeming 20k Hyatt points felt astronomical as that's the same redemption needed for one night at the all-inclusive Hyatt Cabo, and 8k more than the nearby Hyatt Regency SFO.
Verdict: well worth the 20k. This is my new go-to SFO hotel.

Four Seasons Miami

negatives: Limited drawer storage space.
Two elevator systems. You need to take one elevator from the ground floor to the lobby on the 7th floor. Then walk through the lobby to access the 2nd set of elevators for access to the rooms.

The elevator key card system seemed not to be enabled. I was able to access our room floor from the lobby without using my keycard, on several occasions over our three-night stay during different times of the day.

Went to the front desk to inquire about room charges and I was not asked for identification; just room number & last name. After which, still without verifying my identity the front desk agent printed out the folio and handed it to me. This is a safety concern.
The bathroom door is similar to a closet door sans a locking system.

After returning home, we realized we had been charged an extra $80 for breakfast on our last day. We contacted Four Seasons on Saturday morning and after being transferred 3 times were told we would have to call back on Monday when the accounting department was in.
positives: Upon entering the hotel, you immediately notice how all the common areas smell great. Not sure if the area is frequently spritzed or if the scent is in the HVAC system. Either way, it was very delightful while not being overpowering.
The corner room was spacious with two double beds and plenty of natural light.
Large bathroom with soaker tub and great water pressure.
In-room amenities included two robes, two slippers, a coffee machine (LavAzza), a tea kettle along with ceramic mugs, and several drinking glasses.
Great engaging staff from the bellman when we arrived to the front desk agent that checked us in, to the housekeepers that brought requested items.
The hotel has an available text feature (also available via the Four Seasons app) allowing for easy communication and requests.
Guests have complimentary access to the massive Equinox facilities.
Upon entering our room we had a packet that included 4 antiseptic wipes, 2 disposable masks, and a hand sanitizer.

Tested out their "Work from the Leisure" program by requesting a monitor, wireless keyboard, and mouse. All were promptly delivered around 10 am the next day. However, the hotel did not have a USB-C to HDMI adapter for my Mac, nor did I carry any dongles.
Large outdoor pool with plenty of seating.
Two luggage racks! Hotels providing one luggage rack per room is a pet peeve of mine. I was very excited to see two in our room (without having to request it).
Prompt in-room dining. Was able to preorder the night before & breakfast was delivered close to the requested time.
Daily morning coffee station located in the lobby with non-dairy milk options.
Further away from Brickell City Centre (a con for some). The hotel is a walk from Downtown Miami (the last stop on the Miami Metromover Brickell Loop is several blocks away).
Ample seating off the lobby area (7th floor).

The Flag Shinsaibashi is a 3.5-star hotel located in the heart of Osaka, Japan. The hotel is conveniently located near Shinsaibashi Station, making it easy to access all that Osaka has to offer.
The hotel's rooms are spacious and comfortable and are equipped with all the amenities you need for a relaxing stay. The hotel also has a rooftop terrace with stunning views of the city.

negatives: Room Amenities (3): For a Japanese hotel the amenities were lacking. The bathroom only had toothbrushes & hair brushes. The room did not have a coffee machine (located on the 2nd floor) or a robe. The TV was mounted & we were unable to connect our Chromecast & the hotel did not provide TV casting functionality.
The hotel did not have a gym or a pool.
Windows were not sound-proofed. Our 3rd-floor room was directly over the entrance and we heard people talking throughout the day. I am not sure if a room on a higher floor would be better for noise.
Hot breakfast buffet items were tepid in temperature.
Upon check-in, we were told that the room's fire alarm was sensitive & when we showered we should keep the bathroom doors closed or else the alarm would go off.
Upon check-in, we were also told that to ensure the rooms can be quickly turned for the next guest we should not spray perfume in the room.

The seating near the small library was odd. The chairs felt like they were made for toddlers as they were small & rather close to the ground. There is larger "adult" seating near check-in, however, there is a sign that states books should not be removed from the library.
positives: Location (5): Located near Dotonbori, lots of shops & restaurants.
Cleanliness (4.5): There was a rogue zipper in our room along with a little dust on the shelf when we checked in. The room passed the blacklight test.

Service (4): The staff was responsive and the front desk was always staffed. We did not ask for much during our stay. The coffee machine was out of milk one morning, however, we did not notify any staff about it. When we came back later that day the machine was filled. The staff in the restaurant was courteous & cleared dishes quickly while ensuring the buffet was fully stocked.
Bed Comfort (4): Only two pillows were provided and they were smaller and softer than preferred.
Internet (4.5): Internet speed was 38.9. It worked well and did not have any issues with streaming on cell phones.
Onsite coin laundry. Wash (¥300) took 40 minutes and the dryer (¥100) took 30 minutes. The machines did not have weight limits listed, however, we had no issues washing 3 days' worth of clothes.
The breakfast buffet's cold items were very good.
The Deluxe room has 2 Queen sized beds, which was very comfortable.
AC worked well; the room stayed cold.
The hotel had a little library, which was nice.

children.text: If you are looking for an Osaka hotel catering to tourists from the West, located in the heart of Dotonbori, this is a great place to stay.

Overall I was 'meh' about this hotel. While the room was nice & I appreciated the laundry service, it felt lacking in the Japanese culture. I would be unlikely to stay here again unless I needed to be in the vicinity for a specific reason.

negatives: Lack of outlets in the bedroom, most are located next to one nightstand.

negatives: The beach was well-kept, however, there were rocks & seaweed. Ziva's side of the beach was better for entering the water.
The butler-provided phone stopped working towards the end of our stay & we switched to texting the staff, which ended up being a better, faster way of communicating.
positives: Close to the airport. The hotel has a check-in lounge at MBJ Sangster Airport, with a paid shuttle.

children.text: The Hyatt Regency Seattle offers a compelling experience with its prime location, excellent service, and comfortable amenities. While the price point may be high for some, the convenient access to the convention center, responsive staff, and perks like the 8th-floor lounge and Chromecast functionality enhance the stay. Globalist members will find significant value in the complimentary upgrade, breakfast benefit, and waived resort fee. Though minor drawbacks exist, such as the lack of slippers and a slightly worn couch, the stunning views and overall comfort make this hotel a strong contender for travelers seeking a well-located and enjoyable Seattle experience.
The sheltered, winding streets of the Financial District have more Old-World charm than the rest of the city put together. -
The Wall Street Hotel

negatives: Only two elevators which were rather warm during our stay; it did not seem like the fan was working.

The in-room fridge was fully stocked upon arrival. We placed the contents in the cabinet during our stay to be able to use it.

Limited in-room dining. After a few days you can easily go through entire menu & establish your favorites for the remainder of the stay.

TV has YouTube & Netflix (account sign-in necessary) capabilities, so you can stream your favorite shows.
Room is spacious with rather classy color palette. The bathroom has a double vanity and a large enclosed shower.

children.text: After our one-night stay at the
Wynn
, we Ubered to Waldorf Astoria Las Vegas for a one-night stay. After spending one night at the Waldorf Astoria New York when I was a teenager, I was excited to revisit this hotel brand.

We booked a Strip View Room (506 sq ft) through a travel agent and were provided a complimentary upgrade to a Waldorf Junior Suite (646 sq ft). At check-in we were offered an upgrade to a Panorama Strip View One-Bedroom Suite (764 sq ft) for an additional $150, however, we declined.

Our one night cost $480 ($379 rate + $101 taxes and fees) which is an average price for the hotel. We stayed on Thursday night, and weekend rates (Friday/Saturday night) can command upwards of $800 per night plus the taxes and fees.

Sadly, the Waldorf Astoria Las Vegas (previously the Mandarin Oriental Las Vegas) did not live up to my memory of my stay at the Waldorf New York when I was younger. Overall, we had a great stay at a nice hotel with great staff members. With so many hotels in Vegas, we would only stay here again if there was a need to be in the particular vicinity for an event.

children.text: We recently had the pleasure of dining at 3rd & Fernwood and were thoroughly impressed. The food was not only delicious, but beautifully presented, making each dish a feast for the eyes as well as the palate. The service was top-notch; our server was friendly, attentive, and made us feel well-cared for throughout the evening. We also appreciated the clean and inviting atmosphere, which added to the overall enjoyment of our meal. While the prices were perhaps a tad higher than we'd typically prefer, the quality of the food and the overall experience more than justified the cost. We left feeling completely satisfied and are already planning our return visit. 3rd & Fernwood is a true gem and we highly recommend it to anyone seeking a memorable dining experience.
I was excited about Fourk's reopening after the closing news. However as a prior patron I was left feeling a bit underwhelmed.
I've been to the dinner service several times in the past & am not sure if today's experience was a change in the flow going forward or just the new team (day 3 of reopening) working things out.

The introductions started around 10 minutes late & were a bit rushed. While in prior dinners there was an eloquent & elaborate overview of the concept, the flow of the night & the meaning of the paintings on the wall, this most recent dinner was a tad curt & not as engaging as I have come to expect from the evening.

Alexis & her team were cordial but the evening did not exude the homey, communal atmosphere I equate to Fourk. I also found myself explaining the process to my dinner party as they had not been before, something that should have been covered in the intro. Lastly when dishes were cleared the team did not replenish missing cutlery which resulted in the team serving the 3rd course and walking away, unaware we had not way of eating it.
During introductions the chef seemed to struggle on describing what was on the menu for the night, an oddity in my mind. Shouldn't you know the intimate details of the dinner menu?
1st course: Panzanella Salad w/ Balsamic Vinaigrette (8/10) | Nice & fresh, great starter. I don't like capers & enjoyed them very much in this dish. The Salento pairing was nice & not over powering.

2nd course: Sesame-Ginger Ahi Tuna on a Crispy Wonton w/ Avocado Cream, Sriracha Aoli (9.25/10) | Best course of the night. The Chianti was a bit dry for my taste yet paired perfectly with the crispiness of the wontons & balances out the avocado cream & Aoli.

3rd course: Cola Braised Short Rib w/ Fried Shallota & Parmesan White Polenta (6/10) | Worst course of the night. While the polenta was creamy & the rib was tender, the dish came out tepid & was paired with a chilled Syrah which magnified that the gelatinous consistency of the almost cold dish. As the main course this was very disappointing.

4th course: Peach Cobbler w/ Vanilla Ice Cream & Bourbon Caramel Sauce (8/10) | The dessert course was good but I am not sure there was peach in it as it taste more akin of a coffee cake. The prosecco pairing was a bit odd at first but worked well.
Overall a subpar evening (expectation did not match reality). I will wait for the new team to iron out the small details before returning. Note the price increases to $64 (from $54) in September.

"Fourk was created by Executive Chef, Restaurateur and 24-year Military Veteran Paul Jansen. Paul started his culinary journey in 2015 when he left his corporate career of 14 years to start his successful wine bar & tapas concept Citizen Vine. Four years later Paul created Fourk Kitchen, a restaurant concept created to change the way people think about a four-course dining experience, which is usually expensive and sometimes intimidating." - Fourk

children.text: We had a great experience at Tiger Fork DC. While the restaurant is tucked away in an alley, which made it a little tricky to find, the delicious food and drinks were well worth the effort. We started with the Salt & Pepper Calamari, which was perfectly crispy and seasoned. For our main course, we shared the Beef Brisket Chow Fun, and it was fantastic – flavorful with plenty of tender brisket.

We also enjoyed the creative cocktails. The Victoria Harbour was silky smooth and semisweet, while the Nathan Road was a bit stronger but still very enjoyable. The Chinese Kitchen, with its flaming cinnamon stick, was a fun and flavorful experience. The Monkey King Bread was a tasty dessert, though we would have preferred it a bit softer.

The service was friendly and attentive, and the ambiance was pleasant. While the location is a bit unusual, we appreciated the unique atmosphere. We'll definitely be back, especially for happy hour at the bar.

children.text: We always enjoy the fried chicken at Astro. They also have a variety of donuts with interesting flavor combinations, with the Maple Bacon and Key Lime Pie donuts being our favorites. The first night after check-in (4 pm), we headed downstairs to dinner. We were seated immediately outside, next to a nice, cozy fire. Dinner was divine: the chicken thighs ($23) were cooked perfectly & the sauce complimented the meal well. The calamari ($26) was different & the least favorite of the meal. We added prawns ($9) to the flat iron ( $28). While both were good, wished we were given more than 6 prawns.

The following morning around 11 am we went downstairs for lunch. While we were seated immediately the patio was packed & service was a bit slower than the night before. Similar to dinner, lunch was delicious. The soup ($4) was a bit small yet tasty. The Shore Room (TSR) Burger ($16) was delicious with crispy, crunchy fries.
Our final meal was our go-to breakfast: french toast ($14) with a side of eggs ($3) & bacon ($4) along with chicken fried steak ($21).
A delicious end to a delicious trio of meals at The Shore Room. Definitely, a great place to eat in Reno.

children.text: After checking social media & learning about Cosmo's Sunday BOGO 50% off, we decided to try them out. Arriving promptly at 355 pm (they open at 4 pm) allows for the first choice of seating in the intimate dining room. We picked a table near the entrance to the back patio & then promptly went to the counter to order. Overall we had a great experience & would definitely return in the future.

Escape to Andaz Maui at Wailea Resort, a luxurious Hawaiian retreat spanning 15 beachfront acres that is the perfect destination for a well-deserved vacation or a memorable Maui honeymoon. Savor the island spirit with farm-to-table dining, direct access to Mokapu Beach and accommodations offering stunning tropical vistas.

negatives: Beds are a bit softer that we prefer.

There were robes but no slippers in our room upon check-in. We texted the hotel & they stated they are available upon request and brought them up quickly, which felt a bit off putting for a hotel at this price point.
We ordered room service after a long travel day and it included a service fee, $8 delivery charge, along with an automatic tip. Our $92 food bill balloon to nearly $150!

The Ohana Lounge on the first floor is small, dark and was rather warm. Not sure what this space is for, possibly for folks who need a space before check-in or after checking out? I would rather sit in the lobby and take in the view.
More than twice a day we had to log into the wifi; we wished you could sign in your the duration of the stay & not deal with it.
$50 daily resort fee (waived for Globalist) doesn't include [valet] parking (https://www.hyatt.com/andaz/oggaw-andaz-maui-at-wailea-resort/policies)
positives: Gabby, the front desk agent who checked us in was very personable & answered all our questions. She was a great introduction to the high level of hospitality at the resort.
We booked a 2 Queen room for 35k points per night where rates started a around $868++. A few days prior to check-in, I requested a complimentary upgrade to a 2-Queen oceanview, which was granted.
Our room 631, has breathtaking ocean views and was off to the right hand side and 1 floor above the main lobby. Directly above the pools, the balcony was a great people watching spot.
Large bathroom with walk-in shower. Bath products smelled nice but we wish the pumps were a tad longer to allow more product out at once.
Andaz Maui offered $15 F&B credit (or 1k points per night) when you declined housekeeping, which was added to our folio around 5 pm daily.
Great buffet breakfast with fresh juices, rotating pastries and an egg station. It is strange that speciality coffee was an additional charge.

We went to the morning yoga and enjoyed it. We appreciated the free laundry and signed up for the 45-minute photo session. Cacao, our photographer, was great and the smallest package was 20 digital photos for $600.
seoExcerpt: Planning a Maui trip? We stayed at Andaz Maui at Wailea Resort. Gabby at the front desk was amazing and our oceanview upgrade was epic. See our review!
title: Andaz Maui at Wailea Resort Hotel Review

children.text: B﻿ooked a 3-night stay for 35k points per night in a 2 Queen. Prior to check-in, requested a complimentary upgrade to a 2 Queen oceanview which was priced at $1,033 per night.
﻿The staff were amazing, the buffet breakfast delicious, the infinite pools were well maintained and the ocean views were breathtaking.

﻿This is a great Hyatt redemption hotel (35k) as the standard rooms are spacious & the Globalist amenities are plenty. However, the Andaz Maui still has some refinement in some areas (nickel & dining) to justify it's high nightly rate of near $1k.

negatives: With a transit rating of 3.0, some attendees may find public transportation options limited, especially those not familiar with Seattle's transit system.
View from Certain Seats: A rating of 3.0 suggests that some seats may offer obstructed or less-than-ideal views, possibly due to the arena's unique design elements.
While the food quality is high, prices are elevated, with items like mac and cheese priced at $14 and craft beers at $15, which may be steep for some visitors.
positives: Climate Pledge Arena stands out as the world's first net-zero certified stadium, operating entirely on renewable electricity and achieving zero-waste status by diverting over 90% of its waste from landfills.
The arena offers a wide array of culinary choices, including local favorites like Din Tai Fung and Just Poke, with 75% of ingredients sourced within a 300-mile radius.
With a high seat comfort rating of 4.5, attendees can expect a comfortable viewing experience.
Unique Arena Vibes: Scoring 4.25 in arena vibes, the venue boasts features like a 1,700-square-foot living wall and dual-suspended scoreboards, enhancing the overall atmosphere.
The arena includes features like contactless payments and clear signage, contributing to its accessibility rating of 3.5.

children.text: Climate Pledge Arena excels in sustainability, comfort, and atmosphere, making it a premier destination for events in Seattle. While there are areas for improvement, such as transit accessibility and pricing, the arena's commitment to environmental responsibility and guest experience positions it as a leading venue in the industry.​

negatives: Seat comfort (or lack thereof): Okay, let's be real – the seats were ROUGH (2.5/5). Calling it a Spirit flight experience is spot on! I'm only 5'2", and it was a squeeze.
Getting around inside: It was just okay (3.5/5). Not terrible, but not as seamless as maybe some other places.
positives: Being right there at Penn Station is clutch: 5/5 stars for transit, no question.
The energy in MSG is real. Totally electric atmosphere for the Kings vs. Knicks game
The Carnegie Deli Pastrami: 10/10, no notes.
Awesome view from our seats (Sec 112, Row 22). We were right in front of the suites & they shared their snacks with us.

After dropping my pastrami sandwich (tragic!), I went back and purchased another one. At the pickup window the server remembered me and immediately refunded the second sandwich when I told her about the first dropped one. That's incredible service right there.
We did the MSG tour the day prior ($138 for three, rescheduled from game day due to multiple MSG events). Definitely recommend if you want that behind-the-scenes experience.

children.text: The history, the vibe, the easy transit, that pastrami... it mostly outweighed the fact that we felt like sardines in our seats (Seat is smaller than a Spirit flight). Definitely a must-do, especially as NY natives, just maybe prepare for that tight squeeze! While the standard tickets were expensive ($592 for the three tickets), it was still an awesome time at The Garden.

Tip: I signed up for the Knicks Fan First Program newsletter in July 2024 for presale access 10 days before the general public in September 2024.  This was a great way to get "reasonable (to MSG)" ticket prices.
The seating was much better in another section of the arena.

High energy, loud crowd, and a fun in-game atmosphere—likely one of the most engaging stops so far.
Getting to and from the arena was relatively easy, possibly with reliable public transit or ride-share options.
Above-average seats with decent space and support.

children.text: We rolled into Salt Lake City for a weightlifting competition, but couldn’t leave without hitting the Delta Center—which many still know as Vivint Arena. Built strictly for basketball, the seating bowl is incredibly steep, putting you right on top of the action and trapping raw acoustic energy. However, those steep stairs are a legit leg workout, and the upper concourses feel tight. The food is standard and lacks localized flair. The downtown location is also super walkable. It lacks modern sprawl, but the intimate sightlines and loud throwback vibe make it well worth a stop.

It's worth the visit if you're in the area.

negatives: Walls are thin, you can hear everything happening in the hallway: folks walking (running by), children chattering, teenagers giggling and people getting ice. Even worse the elevator dings when it arrives so imagine hearing an iPhone notification sound all through the day and night. There's also an ice machine near the elevator on even floors that adds to the cacophony.

Hotel is mismanaged & there is a lack of communication to guests. We checked in on Monday the 29th around 6 pm. At 1 am on the 30th the fire alarm goes off & we evacuate. We stand outside for around 45 minutes watching the 3 fire trucks unload & reload firefighters.  No one from the hotel came out & spoke to the crowd. I finally went up to the firefighters to ask what happened & they said it was a faulty smoke detector.

Around 8 am, a few hours after fire alarm evacuation, a note is slid under our door to say they are doing fire alarm testing on the 30th, and July 2nd. The note was slid under the door on the 30th, why was this not communicated upon check-in? I assumed it was in response to the fire alarm going off, however later on the front desk agent shared it was a planned annual test.

The fire alarm testing was incessant, every 5 minutes for 4 hours on the 2nd. Then it started again on the 3rd however there was no notification from management regarding the extended hours. When contacted, front desk shared due to occupancy all the rooms were unable to be completed on the 2 days listed and had to be extended. Why was no additional note provided to all guests to alert to the extension?
There is no key card needed to access the elevator, a security concern.
There is no texting functionality, you will need to call or visit the front desk for issues.
Location is not ideal for an extended stay. There is a shopping plaza across the street but it is hard to get around without a car.
Wifi on the weekend lagged significantly (drops to 5 mbps), likely due to high capacity. Ended up hotspotting to my data plan instead and got 40 mbps.

Guests must contend with paper-thin walls, a frustrating lack of transparency during disruptive fire alarm testing, and notable security oversights like unrestricted elevator access. children.text: Overall, Hyatt Place Toronto Airport is a good airport hotel, and we’d stay again. The airport shuttle, Nespresso machine, nearby restaurants, and easy bus access are big pluses. Our biggest issue is the price we’d prefer to see it less than CAD $150 or 7,000 points per night. Between this and our prior stay at the Hyatt House Toronto Airport, we’d choose the Hyatt Place.

negatives: Standard rooms are small, 23 sq m (247 sq feet). Tight for 2 people for an extended stay.
Wall are paper thin. In connecting room 11-177 I heard my neighbour sneeze. In non-connecting room 11166 could hear the entire conversation of next door neighbors at 1130 pm.
In 2019, the 12th through 18th floor were renovated. The furniture in the 12th floor King Standard Room was newer than the furniture in the 11th floor standard room.
After showering, there was a pool of water on the floor.

Each room we tried had different amenities. Our 1st room had an iron, while our 2nd room didn't. Our 1st room had Fairmont branded slippers while our 2nd room had white no brand slippers. All three rooms were the same type "Fairmont King" with 11-1177 and 12-177 being the same layout while 11-166 was a larger footprint.
No turn down service, a hotel of this caliber and price point, should offer twice daily housekeeping.
Breakfast to lunch turnover made the end of breakfast rushed during the weekday. Tip: Come to breakfast 30 minutes earlier.

Luggage storage is on the floor below the lobby. After checking in we were instructed to walk through the lobby, take the elevator downstairs, which seemed weird when the concierge desk is next to the front desk. Expectation is that the bell man would take the bags & store them for us.
positives: Even though small, the bathroom has good counter space.
Were able to request a mini fridge which was delivered to the room promptly.
Nicely appointed gym with 5+ treadmills, 2 stairmaster, a Peloton bike, a rower and 2 rooms with free weights & bench.
Loved that the remodel kept the historical aspects.
Liked the breakfast, simple menu with enough variety across our three-day stay.
Clockwork staff were nice. Drinks were good. Elisabeth at breakfast was nice as well. Cleaner for room 11-177 was great & left personable notes.
Wifi speeds were good, easy to work on laptop from hotel room.
Great location, across the street from Union Staton. Easy to walk to FIFA FanFest, ScotiaBank Arena (Toronto Tempo), and Rogers Centre (BlueJays).

children.text: We loved the Andaz Singapore's central location and the exceptional service we received from the staff. Our room was clean and quiet, and we appreciated the well-stocked mini-bar and effective electronic shades. However, we found the light switches confusing and the bed a bit too firm for our liking. While the rooftop bar, Mr. Stork, and the Cantonese restaurant, 5 on 25, offered delicious food, the gym and pool felt small and crowded, and we felt the hotel was expensive for what it offered and would look to stay somewhere else on subsequent visits to Singapore.

Shiba Park Hotel offers a variety of amenities and services to make guests' stay as enjoyable as possible. The hotel has a rooftop pool with stunning views of the city, a fitness center, and a spa. There are also several restaurants on-site, including a Japanese restaurant, a Western restaurant, and a cafe.

The hotel's rooms and suites are spacious and comfortable and are equipped with all the amenities guests need for a relaxing stay. The hotel also offers a variety of services, such as room service, laundry service, and dry cleaning.

Shiba Park Hotel is the perfect place to stay for both business and leisure travelers. The hotel is conveniently located near many of Tokyo's top attractions and offers a variety of amenities and services to make guests' stay as enjoyable as possible.

children.text: We've stayed twice at Hyatt Regency Lake Tahoe. Once for five (5) nights in February 2021 under their "Work From Hyatt Program" and again for two (2) nights in May 2021.

Under the Work From Home Program, we got 2 connecting rooms, daily breakfast, free parking, and waived resort fees, which are Globalist benefits. The standard King room (1119) was small, however, having the "free" connecting double room (1121) was nice to spread out. Daily breakfast in Sierra Cafe was delicious, we tried many of the dishes, our favorite was the pumpkin pancakes & the fruit plate.
Note: Odd number rooms face the pool, while even numbers face the parking lot. This hotel has 12 floors & we stayed on the 11th floor & had no issues with elevator wait times.
The Family Room (834) was quiet, nice & spacious, located at the end of the 8th-floor hallway with views of the parking lot.

negatives: Room walls are thin, able to hear hallway conversations.

positives: Very personable staff: from Austin at check-in, to Laticia in housekeeping to Kristell in the Sierra Cafe.
Great location on Lake Tahoe, beach access across the street.
Great location in Incline Village, tons of nearby restaurants & shops. Austin's across the street was delicious.

I booked this hotel, via Marriott, for $380 for two nights, inclusive of all fees and taxes. At that price point, and if I got a free upgrade, I would stay here again. However, at the normal rate of $250+/night, this hotel needs renovation before I would consider staying here. At that price point, I will opt to try the Hyatt Regency across from the Ferry Building.

The corner king was nice, however, the bathroom was small & deteriorating. The sink had a large crack in it, and the floor behind the toilet had a puddle after every shower. When we checked in we got two towel sets, I requested more via the Marriott app & they were promptly brought to the room, which was nice.

The TV in the room was annoying, the response time lagged when changing channels. The room had extension cords under one nightstand and the desk. While I appreciate the hotel identifying the lack of power outlets, I would have liked to see a better resolution (updating the side table and desk furniture to have built-in outlets).

children.text: We stumbled upon Atlantic Fish Company just before the dinner rush and snagged a table, but we'd definitely recommend making a reservation, especially for later dining.
Our server, Karina, was an absolute gem! Attentive, friendly, and genuinely personable – she really elevated our experience.
And the food? Amazing! Seriously, we'd travel back to Boston just to savor those flavors again. The branzino was a highlight, and we loved that it came with two sides included.
A few minor observations: the tables for two are a bit cozy (read: small), and the bathroom is down a flight of stairs, which poses an accessibility issue.

But those are minor quibbles in an otherwise fantastic experience. Hot towels at the end of the meal were a lovely touch! Overall, Atlantic Fish Company is a must-try for seafood lovers in the Boston area. Highly recommend!

Take a delicious trip around the world as five acclaimed chefs craft dishes inspired by the flavors and rich traditions of global tea culture. Enjoy tea-inspired cocktails and hand-selected teas from across the globe, guided by a tea sommelier who will pair each chef’s dish with complementary sips—highlighting the nuance, complexity, and culinary connection of tea beyond the cup. and taste how tea has shaped culinary traditions far beyond the cup. negatives: The suite feels to be designed for aesthetic rather than functionality. The safe is in the wardrobe under the hangers limiting ability to hang long jackets, dresses or pants. Aside from the 1 drawer at the wardrobe, there are no place for 1 person to unpack their suitcase, much less a family for a multi night stay.
We were unable to find a light switch that turn off the hallway light. I reached out via text & the person they sent up said we would simply have to close the doors (with the light still on).
Neither bathroom has a full shower door that closes. Who made this design choice & why do so many hotels have it?

The front desk is in a weird nook. When you walk into the lobby, you expect to see the front desk, however you have to turn a corner where there is 1 small table. Imagine the chaos during a busy (3+ persons) checking in.
While I was thanked for my loyalty, there was no welcome amenity or note in the room [upon arrival or anytime there after].
No keycard needed to accesss room floors, a security concern.
The gym is small and in the basement. With 2 treadmills, rowers and ellipticals, free weights and rig there is very little floor space for exercise.
Ordered room service on Friday at 9 pm, quoted 30 minutes and they came at 1005 pm after I called twice from my cell as the room phone was not working.
positives: The suite has several windows that can open. Although most of the windows are blocked by large furniture making it difficult to open them. And the bedroom windows looked directly into apartment next door & thus those blinds stayed closed our entire stay.
The suite has an outdoor patio, which is appreciated, however it can only hold 1 chair so unusable for multiple persons.
$150 per night plus a suite upgrade is a great price for a suite with 2 full bathrooms.
Check-in staff was warm & friendly. Proactively providing hotel amenity information & offering Globalist 4 pm check-out.

TV has streaming connection functionality.

children.text: Get away to the soothing white sands of Poipu Beach on Kauai’s sunny south shore at Grand Hyatt Kauai Resort & Spa. This eco-friendly, luxury beachfront oasis with lush gardens and acres of pools offers ocean view dining, hotel rooms with private lanais, championship golf and Anara Spa.

lounge: yes, paid or member only access
negatives: The hotel is old and shows some wear and tear. Our suite had sections of the wallpaper peeling, and there are tons of wires utilizing the limited outlet space for "modernizing".
Compared to the lounge at the Hyatt Regency Maui, the Grand Club lounge left much to be desired. The food selection was sparse & employee interaction was minimal.

We booked our 4-night stay on points and applied a suite upgrade to a standard suite. No upgrade was provided at check-in; per the front desk agent the highest upgrade possible is to a standard suite, which I already booked. And it would be $350 a night for an ocean view suite, which we declined.
Sprinkler system activates around 7 am and is rather loud.
AC unit in the bedroom is very loud.
Large property that takes a bit of time to learn way finding. I got lost several times during the first two days.
Globalist breakfast is in the lounge with limited options. Would prefer the option is expanded to include room service.

Cash rates do not match the value of a stay; I would not recommend paying cash. Also, the hotel only has 4 standard suites, and they are booked up 18 months in advance. Unless you can secure a standard suite at off-peak point pricing, would not reccomend.
positives: Large gym with two stair masters, an adductor machine & Concept rower that is open 24 hours. It also had a separate room that could be used for stretching.
The Grand lounge is a large space with outdoor seating & is kept clean.
Great view of the ocean from our ground floor room.
Parking in included in the resort fee, a novelty in the world of resort fees.
Suite bathroom has a bidet, a normality in Hawai'i.
Very spacious suite with ceiling fans that worked well at keeping the room cool when the patio door was opened.
Front desk staff is cordial, while other staff (bellman, housekeeping) are very friendly.

Large pools with different sections, including a lazy river. For a pool person, there is plenty of space to spread out. Also, the resort's landscaping is well-maintained, and the pools are part of the resort's aesthetic.
